title: DummyFullstack site tests
sub: Every part of the site, checked by hand: the public pages, accounts and the account page, the contact forms, reviews and the guest book, booking, the newsletter, the blog, the admin area, and the checks that cut across all of it. Each test says who to sign in as, what to do and what you should see, quoting the site's own words.
start:
Run these from the repo root, in two terminals. A reseed puts every account and sample row back the way it is described, which matters because many tests change one (approve it, confirm it, delete it, deactivate it).

cd server
npx prisma db seed   # wipe every table and reseed
npm run dev          # the API on http://localhost:4000

cd client
npm run dev          # http://localhost:5173

npm run dev on the server restarts it whenever a file in src/ changes, and typing rs in its terminal restarts it by hand. Every restart clears the rate limits.

Two addresses. Page links go to the dev server, http://localhost:5173. Tests that need the built, pre-rendered site link to http://localhost:4173 instead: run npm run build, then npm run preview, in client/ first. There is no live site, because the template is never deployed. For a site built from it, set live in site-tests.json and rebuild this page: every page link then gets a live twin.

Password. Every seeded account signs in with 12345678. Register every throwaway account the tests ask for with the same password, so the line above each test holds.

Real inboxes. The three seeded accounts use real gmail.com addresses that belong to strangers. Never send anything to them: no password reset, no email change confirmation, no booking or newsletter in their name. Wherever a test checks an email, use an address you can read. The sample rows (bookings, subscribers, guest book) use example.com addresses, which never deliver anywhere.

Email. Account, contact and booking mail goes out over SMTP, so EMAIL_HOST, EMAIL_PORT and the mailbox settings must be set in the server env (the server will not start without the first two). The newsletter goes through Resend and needs RESEND_API_KEY and an EMAIL_FROM on a domain verified in Resend. Owner notifications go to CONTACT_ADMIN_RECIEVER_EMAIL and BOOKING_ADMIN_RECIEVER_EMAIL, called the owner inbox below. Every email a test expects is named by its subject line.

The browser and the API. FRONTEND_ORIGIN in the server env must list http://localhost:5173, and http://localhost:4173 for the build tests, or the API refuses every call. npm run env:check in server/ names anything missing without printing values.

Rate limits. Each public form allows 5 sends every 15 minutes, password reset and verification emails 5 every 15 minutes, and the whole API 300 requests every 15 minutes. The counts are kept in the server's memory, so restarting the server clears them.

Times. Bookings are in the site's time zone, SITE_TZ in the server env. An invalid name falls back to Europe/London.

Data. npx prisma studio in server/ shows every table. The audit log at /admin/events shows what each action recorded.

Accounts

ForEmailWhat it is
Memberuser@gmail.comUSER, named User. The account page only
Admintom@gmail.comADMIN, named Admin. Every admin page except the audit log. Cannot act on a developer
Developerdev@gmail.comDEVELOPER, named Dev. Everything, including the audit log and granting DEVELOPER

All three are email-verified. Sign-up only ever makes a USER, so the seed is the only way to get the other two. The sample content is in server/prisma/seed/, and each part names the rows it uses.

The statuses, emails and rules these tests check are written up in documents/site/SiteInfo.md.

parts.part: The public site and legal pages
parts.intro: Everything a signed-out visitor sees on the base site: the cookie notice, the home page, the navbar on a wide screen and a phone, the footer, /about, /gallery and its viewer, /faq, /links, /user-agreements, the maintenance page, the 404 page, the loading screen, and the light and dark themes. Signed out throughout, with no account. Nothing is written to the database; the only thing stored is the cookie answer, `CookiePolicy` in this browser's local storage. Use a new private window wherever a test says so, or delete `CookiePolicy` in devtools (Application, Local storage, `http://localhost:5173`) to be asked again. The notice covers every page 10 seconds after a fresh load, so outside the cookie tests answer it once with **I Agree**. Only the home page reviews block needs the server; everything else works with the client alone. Wide screen means at least 1024 pixels, where the navbar shows its links; phone width means devtools device mode at 375 by 667. The forms on these pages (newsletter, reviews, contact) and the pages the navbar leads to are covered by their own parts.

steps.title: Cookie notice: a first visit, after 10 seconds
do: Open a new private window and go to {page:/}.
Watch the page for 10 seconds without pressing anything.
When the notice appears, try to click a link on the page behind it.
Open devtools, Application, Local storage, `http://localhost:5173`.
expect: For the first 10 seconds there is no notice and the page can be used.

After about 10 seconds the page behind is blurred and a box appears in the middle with a cookie picture, the heading **Cookie & Policy Consent**, **Byte Toast Studio** and an underlined link **bytetoast-studio.com**.
Under that: **This website uses cookies, and you must agree to our Terms & Conditions and Privacy Policy to continue.**

Two tick boxes, both unticked: **I consent to the use of cookies for functionality and analytics.** and **I have read and agree to the Terms & Conditions and Privacy Policy.**, where **Terms & Conditions** and **Privacy Policy** are underlined links.
Below them: **If you do not agree or are underage, please exit this site.**
Two buttons side by side, shown in capitals: **I Disagree** (black) and **I Agree** (grey). **I Agree** does nothing while it is grey.
The keyboard focus is on the first tick box.
Nothing on the page behind the box can be clicked.
Local storage has no `CookiePolicy` key yet.
steps.note: The **bytetoast-studio.com** link leaves the local site for the live one. The notice only allows the site to be used once analytics are accepted, and its last line is left over from another template (see found).

steps.title: Cookie notice: the timer runs once per visit
do: In a new private window open {page:/about}.
About 5 seconds later click **FAQ** in the navbar, and wait.
Reload /faq and wait again.
expect: The notice appears about 10 seconds after /about first loaded, so about 5 seconds after you reached /faq: moving to another page does not restart the count.
After the reload the full 10 seconds start again.

steps.title: Cookie notice: keyboard and Escape
do: With the notice open (P1), press Tab repeatedly, then Shift+Tab repeatedly.
Press Space on each tick box, then keep pressing Tab.
Press Escape.
In devtools Elements, find `#cookie-consent-live` and look at its text.
expect: Tab moves only between **bytetoast-studio.com**, the two tick boxes, the **Terms & Conditions** and **Privacy Policy** links and the buttons, and wraps round. It never reaches the page behind.
While **I Agree** is grey, Tab skips it; once both boxes are ticked it turns teal and joins the loop.
Space ticks and unticks the focused box.
Escape does not close the notice.
After Escape, `#cookie-consent-live` (read out by screen readers, not shown) holds **Use the Disagree or I Agree buttons to proceed.**

steps.title: Cookie notice: I Agree
do: With the notice open, tick only the first box and press **I Agree**.
Tick the second box as well and press **I Agree**.
Look at Local storage.
Reload, then open {page:/gallery} and {page:/user-agreements}, waiting 15 seconds on each.
Open {page:/faq} in a new tab of the same private window.
expect: With one box ticked, **I Agree** stays grey and nothing happens.
With both ticked it turns teal, and pressing it closes the box and the blur at once.
Local storage holds `CookiePolicy` with `"agreed":true`, `"version":"1.0.0"`, a `timestamp` and `"assertions":{"acceptCookies":true,"agreeTerms":true}`.
The notice does not come back on reload, on the other pages or in the new tab.
steps.note: Analytics start only after this, and only when `VITE_ANALYTICS_ID` is set in the client env: the cross-cutting part checks that. Delete `CookiePolicy` from local storage to be asked again. For the rest of this part, answer the notice like this once, so it stops covering the pages.

steps.title: Cookie notice: I Disagree
do: In a new private window open {page:/} and wait for the notice.
Press **I Disagree**.
In the same window, type the address {page:/} again and look at Local storage.
Wait 10 seconds.
expect: The tab leaves the site for Google (`https://google.com`).
Nothing was stored: there is still no `CookiePolicy` key.
The notice appears again 10 seconds after the page loads.
steps.note: There is no way to decline analytics and still use the site (see found).

steps.title: Cookie notice on /user-agreements: a bar, not a box
do: In a new private window open {page:/user-agreements} at desktop width and wait 10 seconds.
Scroll the page and click a link in the contents column while the bar is showing.
Narrow the window to phone width (375 pixels).
Tick both boxes and press **I Agree**.
In another new private window open {page:/}, wait for the box, and click **Terms & Conditions** inside it.
expect: No blur and no box: a bar appears at the bottom right on a wide window, and across the bottom at phone width.
The page behind can still be scrolled and clicked.
The bar reads **I consent to cookies for functionality/analytics** and **I agree to the Terms & Conditions and Privacy Policy**, each with a tick box, then **I Disagree** and **I Agree**.
The bar has a solid background, so the legal text does not show through it.
**I Agree** stays grey until both boxes are ticked, then stores the same `CookiePolicy` value as in P4 and the bar goes.
Clicking **Terms & Conditions** in the box opens /user-agreements and the box turns into the bar.
steps.note: The bar has no background colour (see found).

steps.title: Cookie notice while the gallery viewer is open
do: In a new private window open {page:/gallery} and, within 10 seconds, click the first picture to open the viewer.
Wait until the 10 seconds have passed.
Press Escape, then the arrow keys, then Tab.
expect: The cookie box shows on top of the black viewer, where it can be answered.
The keyboard focus is on something you can see.
Escape closes the viewer.
steps.note: The box opens behind the viewer, takes the focus and swallows Escape (see found). The mouse can still close the viewer with its cross.

steps.title: Home page: the hero
do: Open {page:/} at desktop width, then at phone width (375 pixels).
Hover **Book a consultation**, then click it.
expect: The tab reads **Byte Toast Studio | Web Design and Development**.
The heading, in capitals, reads **Byte Toast Studio: web design and development in Tavistock**. It is centred on a phone and left-aligned on a wide screen.
Under it: **Fast, accessible websites and web apps for small businesses, from the first sketch to launch, hosting and ongoing support.**
One teal button with dark text, **Book a consultation** (in capitals). Hovering shows the tooltip **Book a consultation with Byte Toast Studio**.
The hero fills the rest of the first screen below the navbar.
The button opens /booking.

steps.title: Home page: the sections below the hero
do: With the server running on a fresh seed, open {page:/} and scroll slowly down to the footer, at desktop width and at phone width.
Click **More about us**, come back, then click **Read all reviews**.
Come back and press **Book a consultation** and **Send a message** in the last panel.
Stop the server and reload the page.
expect: **What we do** above the heading **Services**, then four bordered cards: **Web Design**, **Web Development**, **SEO** and **Hosting and Support**, each with one sentence (the first is **Clean, accessible designs that work on every screen and make it easy for visitors to get in touch.**). Four across on a wide screen, two on a tablet, one on a phone.

**About the studio** above **Byte Toast Studio in Tavistock**, two paragraphs (the first starts **Byte Toast Studio is a small web design and development studio.**, the second starts **You work with the people who build your site**), the underlined link **More about us**, and a picture (alt text **Placeholder: abstract stacked blocks in ink, terracotta and ochre on paper**), beside the text on a wide screen and under it on a phone.
**More about us** opens /about.

**Reviews** above **What clients say**, then one card: five stars (a screen reader hears **Rated 5 out of 5**), **Great experience**, **Test review seed message (ByteToast Studio).** and **Jamie Rivers**. Below it, the link **Read all reviews** opens /reviews.

A bordered panel: **Ready to start your project?**, **Book a free consultation or send us a message, and we will reply within one working day.**, a teal **Book a consultation** button (/booking) and an outlined **Send a message** button (/contact).
**Stay in the loop** above **Subscribe to our newsletter**, with the fields **Name** (hint **Optional**) and **Email** (red asterisk) and the button **Subscribe**.

With the server stopped the reviews block reads **No reviews yet. Worked with us? We would love to hear how it went.** and its link is **Leave a review**, which opens /reviews. The rest of the page is unchanged.
steps.note: The reviews come from `GET /api/reviews/get-all-reviews`: approved only, newest first, at most three shown. The newsletter form is tested in the newsletter part, and /reviews in the forms part.

steps.title: Home page: the side buttons
do: At desktop width, open {page:/} and look at the left and right edges while the hero fills the window.
Scroll down into the sections.
Hover each side button, then click each.
Scroll back up to the hero.
Open {page:/about}.
expect: While only the hero is in view there are no side buttons.

Once the sections fill most of the window, a strip appears halfway down the left edge with three round icons, tooltips **Byte Toast Studio on Facebook**, **Byte Toast Studio on Instagram** and **Byte Toast Studio on X**.
At the same time a strip appears on the right edge with three icons, tooltips **Booking**, **Contact** and **Gallery**.
The left icons open `https://facebook.com/`, `https://instagram.com/` and `https://x.com/` in a new tab.
The right icons open /booking, /contact and /gallery in the same tab.
Back on the hero both strips disappear.
/about has no side buttons: they are only on the home page.
steps.note: TikTok and Google icons stay hidden while `TIKTOK_URL` and `GOOGLE_BUSINESS_URL` in `client/src/utils/constants/links.js` are empty.

steps.title: Skip link
do: Open {page:/}, click in the address bar, and press Tab once.
Press Enter, then press Tab again.
Do the same on {page:/about}, {page:/faq} and {page:/user-agreements}.
expect: The first Tab shows **Skip to main content** at the top left of the window, over the navbar.
Enter moves the focus to the main content, and the address gains `#main-content`.
On the home page the next Tab lands on **Book a consultation** in the hero.

On /about the next Tab lands on the first footer link (the Facebook icon), because the main content has no links; on /faq it lands on the first question; on /user-agreements on **Terms & Conditions** at the top of the contents column.
On every page the skip link is the first thing Tab reaches.
steps.note: Focus on route change and the single `main` are checked in the cross-cutting part.

steps.title: Navbar on a wide screen, signed out
do: In a window at least 1024 pixels wide, open {page:/}.
Read the links, then click each one in turn, coming back each time.
Click the logo.
expect: The logo is on the left; a screen reader announces it as **Byte Toast Studio homepage**, and it opens the home page.

On the right, two rows of teal links: **Home**, **About**, **Reviews**, **Gallery**, **Contact**, **FAQ**, **Links**, then **Blog**, **Guest Book**, **Booking**, **Newsletter**, **Legal** (with a small down arrow), **Login**, **Sign Up**.
There is no **Account**, no **Admin** and no **Logout**.
There is no menu button at this width.
The links open /, /about, /reviews, /gallery, /contact, /faq, /links, /blog, /guest-book, /booking, /newsletter, /login and /sign-up.
steps.note: The pages behind Reviews, Contact, Blog, Guest Book, Booking, Newsletter, Login and Sign Up belong to their own parts: here, only check that each one opens.

steps.title: Navbar: the current page and hover prefetch
do: At desktop width, open {page:/}, {page:/about}, {page:/faq} and {page:/blog} in turn.
On each, inspect the navbar links in devtools Elements.
Open the Network tab, reload {page:/}, and hover (without clicking) **About**, then **Contact**, then **About** again.
expect: The current page link is blue and the others are teal: **Home** on /, **About** on /about, **FAQ** on /faq, **Blog** on /blog.
The blue link carries `aria-current="page"`; no other navbar link does.
**Home** is never marked on another page.
Hovering **About** fetches `AboutPage.jsx` before any click, and hovering **Contact** fetches `ContactPage.jsx`.
Hovering **About** a second time fetches nothing new.
steps.note: Home, Gallery, FAQ, Links and Blog are in the main bundle, so hovering them fetches nothing. Focusing a link with Tab prefetches in the same way.

steps.title: Navbar: the Legal dropdown on a wide screen
do: At desktop width, on {page:/about}, hover **Legal**, then click it.
Click **Legal** again.
Open it, then click an empty part of the page.
Tab to **Legal**, press Enter, then press Escape.
Press Enter again to open it, press Tab to move onto **Agreements**, and press Escape.
Open it and click **Agreements**.
expect: Hovering alone does not open it.
A click opens a small panel under **Legal** listing **Agreements**, **Terms & Conditions** and **Privacy Policy**, and the button changes from `aria-expanded="false"` to `aria-expanded="true"`.
A second click on **Legal** closes it.
A click on an empty part of the page closes it.
Escape with the focus on **Legal** closes it.
Escape with the focus on a link inside the panel also closes it.
**Agreements** opens /user-agreements.
steps.note: Escape does nothing once the focus is inside the panel (see found).

steps.title: Legal links land on their section
do: At desktop width, on {page:/}, open **Legal** and click **Privacy Policy**.
Go back to {page:/}, open **Legal** and click **Terms & Conditions**.
Now on /user-agreements, scroll to the footer, open **Legal** and click **Privacy Policy**, then open it again and click **Terms & Conditions**.
expect: **Privacy Policy** opens /user-agreements#privacy-policy with the **Privacy & Data** heading at the top of the window.
**Terms & Conditions** opens /user-agreements#terms-and-conditions at **Terms & Conditions for Byte Toast Studio**.
When you are already on /user-agreements, each link scrolls the page to its section.
On /user-agreements all three links in the open panel are blue, as the current page.
steps.note: Both links arrive at the top of the page, and nothing moves at all when you are already on it (see found). The **Privacy Policy** links in the cookie notice go to the same address.

steps.title: Phone menu, signed out
do: Narrow the window below 1024 pixels, or use devtools device mode at 375 by 667, and open {page:/about}.
Press the menu button at the right of the bar.
Press **Legal**, then press it again.
Press the menu button again.
Open the menu and tap **FAQ**.
expect: Below 1024 pixels the links leave the bar: the logo is on the left and a menu button on the right (screen-reader label **Toggle navigation menu**, `aria-expanded="false"`).

Pressing it slides a panel down from the bar with the same links, centred and in the same order: **Home** to **Newsletter**, **Legal** with an arrow, **Login**, **Sign Up**, then the Facebook, Instagram and X icons.
The panel has a solid background: the page underneath does not show through the links.
The button turns into a cross and `aria-expanded` becomes `true`.
**About** is blue and carries `aria-current="page"`.
**Legal** opens a list of **Agreements**, **Terms & Conditions** and **Privacy Policy** under it, and its arrow turns upside down. Pressing it again closes the list.
The cross closes the panel.
Tapping **FAQ** opens /faq with the menu closed.
steps.note: The open panel has no background colour (see found).

steps.title: Phone menu: keyboard and screen reader while closed
do: At 375 pixels wide, open {page:/about} with the menu closed.
Click in the address bar and press Tab repeatedly, watching where the focus goes.
Open the menu with Enter and keep pressing Tab, then close it.
If you have a screen reader, read the page from the top with the menu closed.
expect: With the menu closed, Tab goes skip link, logo, menu button, then on into the page and the footer, with no invisible stops.
With the menu open, Tab moves through the menu links in order.
With the menu closed, a screen reader does not read out the menu links.
steps.note: The closed panel is only faded and moved up, so its links are still in the Tab order (see found).

steps.title: Footer
do: On {page:/about}, scroll to the footer at desktop width and at phone width.
Hover the social icons, then click each icon and each link.
With a screen reader, or devtools Accessibility, check the headings in the footer.
expect: A teal band holding a sky-blue panel with dark text.

Wide: three columns. The logo (alt text **Byte Toast Studio footer logo**) with **Available in Tavistock** and the Facebook, Instagram and X icons; then **Quick Links** and **Services** side by side; then **Contact**. On a phone the blocks stack, with Quick Links and Services still side by side.
**Quick Links**: **Home**, **Contact**, **Login**, **Sign Up**, each opening its page at the top.
**Services**, as plain text: **Web Design**, **Web Development**, **SEO**, **Hosting and Support**.
**Contact**: **Email: hello@bytetoast-studio.com**, **Phone: 07846286385 (UK)**, then **Location:** with **70 Monksmead**, **Tavistock**, **PL19 8ER** and **United Kingdom** on separate lines.
Below the panel, a strip: **© 2026 Byte Toast Studio** and **Website by Byte Toast Studio**.

The icons have tooltips **Byte Toast Studio on Facebook**, **Byte Toast Studio on Instagram**, **Byte Toast Studio on X**, and open `https://facebook.com/`, `https://instagram.com/` and `https://x.com/` in a new tab.
**Byte Toast Studio** in the credit is underlined and opens `https://bytetoast-studio.com` in a new tab.
A screen reader announces the headings **Quick Links**, **Services** and **Contact**.
The same footer is on the home page and /user-agreements.
steps.note: FAQ, links, maintenance and the 404 page have no footer, and the gallery has its own shorter block (P23). The **Services** and **Contact** headings are empty to a screen reader (see found).

steps.title: Footer: the email and phone links
do: In the footer, click the email line.
Inspect the email and phone lines in devtools Elements.
On a phone (or a desktop with a calling app), tap the phone line.
expect: The email opens a new message to `hello@bytetoast-studio.com`; a screen reader announces it as **Email Byte Toast Studio**.
A screen reader announces the phone line as **Call Byte Toast Studio**.
The phone link is `tel:` followed by a number that dials, such as `07846286385` or `+447846286385`.
Tapping it offers to call 07846286385.
steps.note: The link is `tel:+07846286385`, which no phone can dial (see found).

steps.title: About page
do: Open {page:/about} at desktop, tablet and phone widths.
In devtools Elements, select the `main` element.
expect: The tab reads **About | Byte Toast Studio**.
The heading **About Byte Toast Studio** (in capitals), then **We deliver clean builds, clean SEO, and clean results for clients across United Kingdom.**

**Our story**: **Byte Toast Studio was founded on a simple idea: do great work, communicate clearly, and make the process effortless.** and **From discovery through launch and beyond, we combine practical strategy with reliable execution across Web Design, Web Development, SEO, Hosting and Support.**

**Mission & values**: three bordered cards, **Clarity** (starting **Transparent scope, milestones, and updates**), **Craft** (**Clean, accessible builds aligned with performance and SEO.**) and **Care** (**Respect for users, your brand, and long-term maintainability.**). One column on a phone, two on a tablet, three on a wide screen.
**How we work**: **1. Discovery**, **2. Plan**, **3. Build** and **4. Launch & support**, each with a line under it, the first **Define goals, constraints, and success criteria together.**
The footer follows.
`main` has `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` pointing at elements that exist on the page.
steps.note: They point at `about-main-heading` and `about-main-desc`, which do not exist (see found).

steps.title: Gallery page
do: Open {page:/gallery} at desktop, tablet and phone widths.
Hover a picture, then Tab through the pictures.
expect: The tab reads **Gallery | Byte Toast Studio**.
**Recent work** (in capitals), the heading **Gallery**, then **Photos of recent projects from Byte Toast Studio and the studio behind them. Select any image to see it larger.**
Eight pictures, each in a 3 by 4 frame: three columns on a wide screen, two on a tablet or phone.
The first is **Placeholder: sketch of a website with a hero banner and three feature cards** (alt text) and the last **Placeholder: abstract stacked blocks in ink, terracotta and ochre on paper**.
Hovering a picture zooms it in slightly within its frame.
Each picture is a button: a screen reader announces **Open image 1 of 8** through **Open image 8 of 8**.
There are no filter or category buttons.
There is no **Loading more images** line: it only shows while more than 12 pictures remain to be loaded.

steps.title: Gallery viewer
do: On {page:/gallery}, click the first picture.
Press the right arrow key nine times, then the left arrow key twice. Use the round arrow buttons as well.
Press Tab and Shift+Tab several times.
Try to scroll the page, and click the black area around the picture.
Hover the cross and each round button.
Press Escape.
Tab to the third picture, press Enter, then click the cross.
expect: A black screen covers the window, with the picture as large as fits, a white cross at the top right and blue round buttons with arrows at the left and right.
The focus starts on the cross (screen-reader label **Close**).

The right arrow key and the **Next image** button step forward; after the eighth picture comes the first again. The left arrow key and **Previous image** step back, wrapping from the first to the eighth.
Tab and Shift+Tab move only between the cross and the two round buttons.
The page behind does not scroll, and clicking the black area does nothing.
Hovering a control keeps its icon visible.
Escape closes the viewer and the focus goes back to the first picture.
The cross closes it too, with the focus back on the third picture.
steps.note: Hovering turns each control white on white (see found).

steps.title: Gallery: the block under the pictures
do: Scroll to the bottom of {page:/gallery}.
Click each icon and each link.
expect: There is no site footer. Instead a centred blue block reads **Follow us on** in large letters, with the Facebook, Instagram and X icons under it.
Then the links **Home**, **Contact**, **Login** and **Sign Up**, which open /, /contact, /login and /sign-up.

Then **Byte Toast Studio**, **Tavistock**, **© 2026 Byte Toast Studio. All rights reserved.**, **Unauthorized use or reproduction of content is strictly prohibited.** and **Website by Byte Toast Studio**.
The icons open `https://facebook.com/`, `https://instagram.com/` and `https://x.com/` in a new tab, and **Byte Toast Studio** in the credit opens `https://bytetoast-studio.com` in a new tab.

steps.title: FAQ page
do: Open {page:/faq} at desktop and phone widths.
In devtools Elements, select the `main` element.
expect: The tab reads **FAQ | Byte Toast Studio**.
Small capitals above the heading, the heading **Frequently Asked Questions**, and an introduction that fits a web design studio.

Eight questions, each in a bordered box with **+** at the right, all closed: **How much does a website cost?**, **How long does it take to build a website?**, **What do you need from me to get started?**, **Do you provide hosting and domains?**, **Will my website work on phones and tablets?**, **Will my website show up on Google?**, **Can I update the website myself?**, **What happens after my website goes live?**
No answer text shows until a question is opened.
`main` has `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` pointing at elements that exist on the page.
There is no site footer on this page.
steps.note: The small capitals read **Before You Approach** and the introduction starts **Read this first. Most questions are answered here**, then **including how to approach, what is expected, and how to engage properly.**: copy left from another template. `main` points at `faq-main-heading` and `faq-main-desc`, which do not exist (see found).

steps.title: FAQ: opening and closing the answers
do: On {page:/faq}, click **How much does a website cost?**.
Click **How long does it take to build a website?**.
Click it again.
Tab to **Can I update the website myself?** and press Enter, then Space.
Inspect a question in devtools Elements, open and closed.
expect: The first answer slides open under the question: **Every project is quoted individually after a short call, because the price depends on the number of pages, features such as bookings or a shop, and how much content you already have. You get a fixed quote before any work starts.** Its **+** becomes a minus sign.
Opening the second question closes the first: only one answer is open at a time.
Clicking an open question closes it again.

Enter opens the focused question and Space closes it. Its answer is **Yes. Blog posts, newsletters, bookings and messages are managed from a simple admin area, and Byte Toast Studio can make other changes for you on a support plan.**
Each question is a button with `aria-expanded` `true` when open and `false` when closed, and `aria-controls` naming its answer (`faq-answer-0` for the first).

steps.title: Links page
do: Open {page:/links} at desktop, tablet and phone widths.
expect: The tab reads **Links | Byte Toast Studio**.

parts.intro: Signing up, signing in and out, **Keep me logged in**, the email verification link and the resend button, forgotten and reset passwords, the guards that send a signed-out visitor to /login and back again, a deactivated account, and the nav a USER sees. Run the tests in order: later ones use the accounts and emails that earlier ones make. You need two addresses you can read, best as plus aliases of your own inbox: Account A (for example `you+a@gmail.com`) and Account B (for example `you+b@gmail.com`). Both sign up with the password `Toast1!ab`; A25 resets Account A's to `Toast2!ab`. The seeded `user@gmail.com` and `tom@gmail.com` are only signed in to: they are real inboxes belonging to strangers, so never ask for a reset or a verification email for them. Account mail goes over SMTP from `USER_VERIFY_EMAIL` and `USER_RESET_EMAIL`; without those settings every page still works but nothing arrives. Its links point at http://localhost:5173 while `NODE_ENV` is not `production`, so open them on the computer running the dev server. Several tests need a second browser: use a private window. Rate limits live in the server's memory, so restarting the server clears them: the forgot password form and the resend button take 5 requests per 15 minutes, and sign-in, sign-up, change password and change email take 3 within 10 seconds. Past either limit the form says **Too many requests. Please try again later.** Log out before any test with a different `who`. The account-page part carries on with both accounts, so reseed (`npx prisma db seed` in `server/`, which wipes every table) only once both parts are done.

steps.title: /sign-up: what the form shows
do: Open {page:/sign-up} in a window at least 1024px wide.
Look at the nav bar at the top.
Press the eye button in **Password**, then press it again.
Click **terms and conditions** in the tick box line, then go back.
Click **Login Now**.
expect: The tab reads **Sign Up | Byte Toast Studio**.
The page heading reads **Join Byte Toast Studio**, and the box below it is headed **Sign Up Now**.
Under the box heading: **All fields are required. Use a valid email and a strong password.**
The fields, in order: **Username** (hint **Choose a unique username.**), **Email** (hint **Enter a valid email address.**), **Password**, **Confirm Password** and **Country**.
The **Password** hint reads **Password must be at least 8 characters, include 1 uppercase letter, 1 number, 1 special character, and cannot contain / or \.**
The **Confirm Password** hint reads **Re-enter your password. It must match and meet the same requirements.**
**Country** starts on **United Kingdom**.
The box **I agree to all terms and conditions.** is already ticked.
The eye button shows the password as plain text, its label changing from **Show password** to **Hide password**, and hides it again.
**terms and conditions** opens /user-agreements.
The button reads **Register Now**, and under it **Already a member?** is followed by **Login Now**, which opens /login.
The nav ends with **Login** and **Sign Up**, and has no **Account**, **Logout** or **Admin**.
steps.note: **Username** is saved as the display name and nothing checks that it is unique, and the **Country** choice is never sent to the server (found).

steps.title: /sign-up: password rules checked in the browser
do: Open devtools on the Network tab.
On {page:/sign-up}, type `Tester A` in **Username**, Account A's address in **Email**, `password` in both password fields, and press **Register Now**.
Type one more letter at the end of **Username**, then delete it.
Put `Toast1!ab` in **Password** and `Toast1!ac` in **Confirm Password** and press **Register Now**.
Put `Toast1!a"` (ending in a double quote) in both password fields and press **Register Now**.
expect: **Password must be at least 8 characters, include 1 uppercase letter, 1 number, and 1 special character, and cannot contain / or \.** shows in red, centred under **Register Now**.
**Username**, **Email**, **Password** and **Confirm Password** get a red ring while the message shows.
Focus moves to the red message.
Typing in any field clears the message and the red rings.
Mismatched passwords give **Passwords do not match or fail requirements. Please re-enter them.**
The password ending in `"` is refused with the first message, which names only / and \ as not allowed.
The Network tab shows no request to `/api/auth/sign-up/email`.
steps.note: The message about quotes is in found.

steps.title: /sign-up: the terms box
do: On {page:/sign-up}, fill **Username** `Tester A`, Account A's address and `Toast1!ab` in both password fields.
Untick **I agree to all terms and conditions.** and press **Register Now**.
expect: **You must agree to the terms and conditions to continue.** shows in red under **Register Now**.
No request to `/api/auth/sign-up/email` is sent.
You stay on /sign-up, signed out.

steps.title: /sign-up: an empty Username or a malformed Email
do: On {page:/sign-up}, leave **Username** empty, type Account A's address in **Email** and `Toast1!ab` in both password fields, keep the box ticked and press **Register Now**.
Wait 10 seconds. Type `Tester A` in **Username**, change **Email** to `not-an-email` and press **Register Now**.
Wait 10 seconds. Clear **Email** and press **Register Now**.
expect: With no username the form is sent, and the server's text shows in red: **[body.name] Too small: expected string to have >=1 characters**
The cursor moves to **Username**.
With `not-an-email` the message is **[body.email] Invalid email address**
With **Email** empty the message is the same **[body.email] Invalid email address**, and the cursor moves to **Email**.
No `User` row is created in Prisma Studio.
steps.note: This is what the code does today: the browser should stop an empty or malformed field with a plain message before anything is sent (found). Each press counts towards the sign-up limit of 3 in 10 seconds, hence the waits.

steps.title: /sign-up: creating Account A
do: On {page:/sign-up}, enter **Username** `Tester A`, Account A's address and `Toast1!ab` in both password fields. Leave **Country** and the tick as they are and press **Register Now**.
Look at the nav.
Open devtools, Application, Local storage, http://localhost:5173.
Run `npx prisma studio` in `server/` and open `User`, then `Account` and `Session`.
expect: The button shows a spinner while it works.
You land on /account, heading **Your account**, with **Signed in as** and Account A's address under it.
The **Email** card reads **Your email address isn't verified yet. Check your inbox for the link, or send a new one.**
Under that notice is a **Resend verification email** button.
The nav shows **Account** and **Logout** in place of **Login** and **Sign Up**.
The nav has no **Admin** dropdown.
Local storage holds `isLoggedIn` = `true`.
`User` has a new row with the address in lower case, `name` `Tester A`, `role` `USER`, `emailVerified` false, `isActive` true and `image` empty.
`Account` has a row for the new user with `providerId` `credential`.
`Session` has one row for the new user.
steps.note: Keep Account A for the rest of this part and the account-page part.

steps.title: The verification email
do: Open Account A's inbox and find the email that A5 sent (it goes out a few seconds after the page answers).
Click the `bytetoast-studio.com` link in the footer.
expect: The subject is **Byte Toast Studio: Verify email address**.
It comes from **Byte Toast Studio** at the `USER_VERIFY_EMAIL` address.
The logo at the top loads from `https://bytetoast-studio.com/brand/logo.png`.
The heading reads **Confirm your email address**, with Account A's address under it.
The text reads **Click the button below to confirm this address for your Byte Toast Studio account. If you didn't request this, you can ignore this email.**
A bold line **Link expires on** gives a date and time 24 hours after sign-up, in UK time (for example `19 Oct 2026, 14:05`).
A green **Verify Email Address** button.
Under it **If the button doesn’t work, copy and paste this link into your browser:** and the link written out, of the form `http://localhost:5173/verify-email-address/<user id>/<token>`.
The footer shows `bytetoast-studio.com` and **© 2026 Byte Toast Studio. All rights reserved.**
The footer link opens the site at `https://bytetoast-studio.com`.
steps.note: Do not press the button yet: A17 uses this link. Today the footer link has no `https://`, so it opens nothing (found).

steps.title: Log out
do: At a width of at least 1024px, press **Logout** at the right end of the nav.
Look at local storage and the `Session` table.
Open {page:/account}.
expect: You land on the home page, heading **Byte Toast Studio: web design and development in Tavistock** (shown in capitals).
The nav shows **Login** and **Sign Up** again, with no **Account** or **Logout**.
`isLoggedIn` is gone from local storage.
Account A's row in `Session` is gone.
/account sends you to /login.

steps.title: /sign-up: an address that already has an account
do: On {page:/sign-up}, enter **Username** `Someone`, Account A's address and `Toast1!ab` in both password fields, and press **Register Now**.
Wait 10 seconds and press it again with the address in capitals (for example `YOU+A@GMAIL.COM`).
expect: **User already exists. Use another email.** shows in red under **Register Now**.
Focus moves to the message.
The capitalised address gets the same message.
You stay on /sign-up, signed out.
No second `User` row appears.
No email arrives at Account A's address.
steps.note: Unlike forgot password, sign-up does say that an address is taken. That is Better Auth's own reply.

steps.title: /login: the page
do: Open {page:/login}.
Click **Forgot password?**, then go back.
Click **Sign up now!**, then go back.
expect: The tab reads **Login | Byte Toast Studio**.
The heading reads **Sign in to your account**.
**Email** has the hint **Enter the email you used to sign up.** and the placeholder `name@email.com`.
**Password** has the hint **Password is required.** and an eye button.
**Keep me logged in** starts unticked.
**Forgot password?** opens /forgot-password.
The button reads **Sign in**.
Under it **Don’t have an account yet?** is followed by **Sign up now!**, which opens /sign-up.

steps.title: /login: wrong details
do: On {page:/login}, press **Sign in** with both fields empty.
Wait 10 seconds. Sign in as Account A with the password `Wrong1!pass`.
Wait 10 seconds. Sign in as `nobody-here@example.com` with `Toast1!ab`.
expect: Empty fields give **Invalid email** in red under **Sign in**.
The cursor moves to **Email**.
The wrong password gives **Invalid email or password**, with the cursor in **Email**.
The unknown address gives the same **Invalid email or password**, so the page does not reveal whether an account exists.
Both fields get a red ring while a message shows.
Typing in either field clears the message and the rings.
You stay on /login, signed out.
steps.note: Sign-in allows 3 presses in 10 seconds (A13), hence the waits.

steps.title: /login: signing in, and the nav afterwards
do: On {page:/login}, sign in as Account A with `Toast1!ab`.
Look at the nav at a width of at least 1024px.
Narrow the window below 1024px and press the menu button at the top right.
Click **Account**.
Open {page:/login} again.
Look at the `Session` table.
expect: The button shows a spinner, then you land on the home page.
The desktop nav ends **Legal**, **Account**, **Logout**.
The desktop nav has no **Login**, **Sign Up** or **Admin**.
The phone menu lists the same links, with **Logout** at the bottom and no **Admin**.
**Account** opens /account.
/login sends you straight to the home page while you are signed in.
`Session` has a new row for Account A.

steps.title: Keep me logged in
do: Log out. On {page:/login}, leave **Keep me logged in** unticked and sign in as Account A.
In devtools, Application, Cookies, http://localhost:5173, look at `better-auth.session_token` and `better-auth.dont_remember`, and at the new row in `Session`.
Log out, tick **Keep me logged in** and sign in again.
Look at the cookies and the `Session` row again.
expect: Unticked: `better-auth.session_token` expires at **Session**, so it ends when the browser closes.
Unticked: a `better-auth.dont_remember` cookie is present.
Unticked: the `Session` row's `expiresAt` is one day ahead.
Ticked: `better-auth.session_token` expires 7 days ahead.
Ticked: there is no `better-auth.dont_remember` cookie.
Ticked: the `Session` row's `expiresAt` is 7 days ahead.
steps.note: Cookies ignore the port, so the API's cookies from localhost:4000 show under localhost:5173. Tick the box whenever you sign in for the rest of the tests.

steps.title: Sign-in limit: 3 within 10 seconds
do: Log out and open {page:/login}.
Sign in as Account A with `Wrong1!pass` four times as fast as you can.
Wait 10 seconds and sign in with `Toast1!ab`.
expect: The first three presses answer **Invalid email or password**.
The fourth answers **Too many requests. Please try again later.** in red.
After the wait the right password signs you in.
steps.note: The count is kept by the server for each address requests come from, not per account: locally every browser, private windows included, shares one count. Sign-up, change password and change email have the same limit, each counted separately.

steps.title: Resend the verification email (Account B)
do: Log out. On {page:/sign-up}, register Account B: **Username** `Tester B`, Account B's address, `Toast1!ab` in both password fields.
On /account, in the **Email** card, press **Resend verification email**.
Open Account B's inbox.
expect: Registering lands on /account with the not-verified notice in the **Email** card.
The button shows a spinner, then **Verification email sent to** and Account B's address appear in green under it.
Two emails arrive, both **Byte Toast Studio: Verify email address**: one from sign-up and one from the button.
The two links have different tokens.
steps.note: Do not open either link before A16.

steps.title: Resend limit: 5 per 15 minutes
do: Restart the server (`npm start` in `server/`) so the count starts at zero, and reload /account.
Press **Resend verification email** five times, waiting each time for the green message.
Press it a sixth time.
Restart the server again and press it once more.
expect: Each of the first five presses shows **Verification email sent to** and the address in green.
Five more emails arrive in Account B's inbox.
The sixth press shows **Too many requests. Please try again later.** in red under the button.
No email arrives for the sixth press.
After the restart the button sends again.
steps.note: Sends real emails to Account B's inbox. The count is per address requests come from, not per account (locally every browser shares it), and a restart clears it.

steps.title: Verification link: a fresh link, signed out
do: Open a new private window and paste Account B's newest verification link into it.
Wait 5 seconds.
In Prisma Studio, look at Account B's `User` row and at `Session`.
expect: The tab reads **Verify Email | Byte Toast Studio**.
The heading starts as **Verifying Your Email Address**, with a spinner and **Verifying your email address. Please wait while we complete the verification process.**
The heading changes to **Email Successfully Verified**.
**Your email has been verified successfully.** in bold, then **You can continue now.** with a countdown from 5 seconds.
Two buttons: **Go to Home** and **Go to Account**.
The private window is now signed in as Account B: its nav shows **Account** and **Logout**.
After the countdown you land on /account, where the **Email** card reads **Your email address is verified.** in green.
`emailVerified` is now true.
`Session` has a new row for Account B.
steps.note: Opening an unused link signs that browser in, though nobody typed a password there. Close the private window afterwards.

steps.title: Verification link: opened while signed in
do: In your normal window, log out and sign in as Account A.
Open the A6 link in the same window and wait 5 seconds.
expect: **Email Successfully Verified**, with **Go to Home** and **Go to Account**.
The countdown ends on /account, where the **Email** card reads **Your email address is verified.**
Account A's `emailVerified` is true.
No extra `Session` row appears: the current session is kept.

steps.title: Verification link: one already used
do: Log out and open the A6 link again.
Sign in as Account A and open the link once more.
expect: Signed out, it still shows **Email Successfully Verified**.
Signed out, the buttons are **Go to Home** and **Go to Login**, and the countdown ends on /login.
It does not sign you in: the nav still shows **Login** and **Sign Up**.
Signed in, it shows **Email Successfully Verified** with **Go to Account**.
Nothing changes in `User` or `Session`.
steps.note: A verification link is not used up by opening it. It keeps working until it expires 24 hours after it was sent.

steps.title: Verification link: a broken or expired link
do: Log out. Take the A6 link, change the last five characters of the token and open it.
Press **Retry**.
Press **Go to Home**, go back, and press **Go to Login**.

**There was an issue verifying your email. Your link may be invalid or expired.** in bold red.
Three buttons: **Retry**, **Go to Home** and **Go to Login**.
Below them: **If the issue persists, request a new verification link or contact support.**
There is no countdown and the page stays put.
**Retry** shows the same failure.
**Go to Home** opens the home page and **Go to Login** opens /login.

steps.title: /forgot-password: the page

expect: The tab reads **Forgot Password | Byte Toast Studio**.
The heading reads **Forgotten your password?**, with **Request a reset** under it.
One field, **Email**, with the hint **Enter the email you used to sign up.**
The button reads **Submit**.

steps.title: /forgot-password: the same reply for any address, and the email
do: On {page:/forgot-password}, enter Account A's address and press **Submit**.
Change the address to `nobody-here@example.com` and press **Submit**.
Look at the `Verification` table.
Open Account A's inbox.
expect: Both presses show **If an account exists for that email, a reset link has been sent.** in green under **Submit**.
Typing in the field clears the message.
`Verification` has one new row, whose `identifier` starts `reset-password:`.
One email arrives, at Account A only, with the subject **Byte Toast Studio: Reset Password**.
It comes from **Byte Toast Studio** at the `USER_RESET_EMAIL` address.
It reads **Password reset request**, then **Hello** and Account A's address.
Then **We received a request to reset the password for your Byte Toast Studio account.**
A bold line **This link expires on** gives a time one hour ahead, in UK time.
A green **Reset your password** button, and the link written out, of the form `http://localhost:5173/reset-password/<user id>/<token>`.
It ends by saying you can ignore the email if you did not ask, above the same `bytetoast-studio.com` footer as the verification email.

steps.title: /forgot-password: an empty or malformed address

Type `abc` and press **Submit**.
expect: Both show **[body.email] Invalid email address** in red under **Submit**.

parts.intro: The /account page: the Profile card (avatar and display name), the Email card (changing the address), the Password card, the Devices card and Delete account. It follows the accounts part and uses its two accounts: Account A (password `Toast2!ab` after A25) for everything but the delete, and Account B (`Toast1!ab`), which U21 deletes. U7 moves Account A to a second address you can read (for example `you+a2@gmail.com`), and U10 and U11 change its password to `Toast3!ab`, then `Toast4!ab`. Keep a private window to hand as the other device. Avatars need the `STORAGE_*` settings on the server and `VITE_MEDIA_CDN` on the client. Have a PNG and a JPEG under 5 MB, a JPEG over 5 MB, an SVG and a PDF ready. Use your storage provider's console to look in the bucket: every avatar sits under `testing/avatars/<user id>/`. The **Resend verification email** button on this page is tested in the accounts part (A14, A15). Change password and change email allow 3 presses in 10 seconds, so pause between quick retries. A reseed removes both accounts.

parts.part: Contact, callback, reviews and the guest book
parts.intro: The public forms, signed out throughout: /contact with its contact form (and an optional photo) and its callback form, /reviews with its form and the list of approved reviews, and /guest-book with its form and the wall of approved messages. Every send adds a row to `ContactForm`, `CallbackForm`, `Review` or `GuestBookMessage`, and a photo adds a `MediaItem` row and a file under `testing/contact/` or `testing/guestbook/` in the bucket. Part admin-inbox approves, edits and deletes what this part creates, so keep the rows until you have run it; `npx prisma db seed` in `server/` puts the seeded rows back afterwards, but it does not delete files from the bucket. Contact and callback sends email the owner inbox (**New Contact Form Received**, **New Callback Request**); the visitor is sent nothing, and reviews and guest book messages send no mail at all. Type your own address wherever a form asks for one. The photo tests need the `STORAGE_*` settings in the server env, bucket CORS that allows `http://localhost:5173`, and `VITE_MEDIA_CDN` in the client env for photos on the guest book wall. Each form allows 5 sends per 15 minutes from one connection, counted separately for each form: restart the server before each rate limit test (F10, F14, F20, F30), and whenever a form refuses you in the middle of another test. `npx prisma studio` in `server/` shows what each send stored.

steps.title: Contact form: a message without a photo
do: On {page:/contact}, fill **First Name**, **Last Name**, your own address in **Email** (with a capital letter in it), `07700 900456` in **Mobile**, leave **Phone** and the three address boxes empty, and write a message of a few lines.
With the Network tab open, press **Submit**.
Type a letter in **First Name**.
In Prisma Studio, open `ContactForm`.
expect: While it sends, the button reads **Submitting** with three dots and is greyed out.
Green text under the button: **Form submitted successfully!**
Every box empties.
Typing again removes the green text.
`POST /api/contact/create-new-contact-form` answers 201.
`ContactForm` has a new row with your names, mobile and message, with `phone`, `streetAddress`, `city`, `postcode` and `imageKey` all null.
The stored `email` is all lower case.
steps.note: A message over 2,000 characters is stored cut short, with no warning (see found). The owner email for this send is checked in F6.

steps.title: Contact form: the owner email
do: After F5, open the owner inbox and open **New Contact Form Received**.
Click the email address inside it, then cancel the new mail.
Click the link in its footer.
Press Reply and look at the To line.
expect: The subject is **New Contact Form Received**, from **Byte Toast Studio** at the `CONTACT_ADMIN_EMAIL` address.
A green heading **New Contact Form Submission**, then **Hi, you’ve received a new message from your website:**
A grey box lists **First Name:**, **Last Name:**, **Email:** (your address, as a mail link) and **Mobile:** with what you typed.
There is no **Phone:**, **Address:**, **City:** or **Postcode:** line, because those boxes were left empty.
**Message:** shows your message, then **Submitted:** gives the date and time, for example `18 Oct 2026, 14:05`.
There is no **Attached Image:** line.
Below the box: **Be sure to follow up promptly to keep things moving!**
The footer shows **Byte Toast Studio**, a link **bytetoast-studio.com** that opens https://bytetoast-studio.com, and **© 2026 Byte Toast Studio. All rights reserved.**
Reply addresses the answer to the visitor's address.
Your own inbox receives nothing: the visitor gets no acknowledgement.
steps.note: Today the footer link has no `https://`, so it does not open the site, and Reply goes to the site's own contact mailbox because the email sets no Reply-To (see found). If `CONTACT_ADMIN_RECIEVER_EMAIL` or the contact mailbox settings are missing, nothing arrives but the form still says it was sent, and the audit log records **Failed to send contact form notification email.**

steps.title: Contact form: choosing, changing and removing a photo
do: On {page:/contact}, open the Network tab, click the dashed box and choose a JPEG or PNG under 5MB.
Press **Change** and choose a different image.
Press **Remove**.
Drag a PDF from your desktop onto the dashed box.
Click the box and choose an image larger than 5,242,880 bytes (a 6MB photo will do).
Choose a JPEG under 5MB again.
Remove it, press Tab until the dashed box has focus, and press Enter.
expect: The dashed box is replaced by a preview of the picture (alt text **Selected attachment preview**), with a teal **Change** button and a red **Remove** button under it.
**Change** reopens the picker, and the preview swaps to the new picture.
**Remove** brings the dashed box back.
The PDF shows **Only images are allowed.** in small red italics under the small print, and no preview.
The large image shows **File too large (>5MB).** the same way, and no preview.
Choosing a good image clears the red message.
Enter on the focused box opens the picker (Space does too).
Nothing is uploaded yet: no request to `presign-url` appears until you press **Submit**.
steps.note: The picker hides PDFs, so drag one in to see the refusal. The limit is 5MB counted in binary (5,242,880 bytes), the same figure the server checks after the upload.

steps.title: Contact form: sending with a photo
do: On {page:/contact}, fill **First Name** `Photo`, **Last Name** `Tester`, your own address and a short message, and choose a JPEG under 5MB.
Open the Network tab and press **Submit**.
In Prisma Studio, open `MediaItem` and `ContactForm`.
Open the new **New Contact Form Received** in the owner inbox.
expect: Four requests run in order: `POST /api/media-services/presign-url` (200, with a `url`, a `key`, a `publicUrl` and `maxBytes` of 5242880), a `PUT` to the storage host (200), `POST /api/media-services/confirm-upload` (200, with `bytes`), then `POST /api/contact/create-new-contact-form` (201).
**Form submitted successfully!** shows, the boxes empty and the dashed box comes back.

`MediaItem` has a row with `resource` `contact`, `kind` `IMAGE`, `visibility` `PUBLIC`, `bytes` filled in, your file name in `originalFilename`, and a `key` starting `testing/contact/anon/` followed by the year and month.
The new `ContactForm` row for Photo Tester has that key in `imageKey`.
The email has an **Attached Image:** line with the picture shown in the email.
steps.note: Keep this row: part admin-inbox shows the photo (I5, I6) and deletes it with the form (I8). The file is in a public bucket, so anybody with its address can open it. Signed in, the key carries your user id in place of `anon`.

steps.title: Contact form: picture types the server refuses
do: On {page:/contact}, fill the form validly, choose a `.bmp` or `.avif` picture, open the Network tab and press **Submit**.
Press **Remove**, choose an `.svg` file and press **Submit**.
In Prisma Studio, look at `ContactForm` and `MediaItem`.
expect: The picker offers the BMP or AVIF, and the form shows its preview.
On **Submit**, `presign-url` answers 400 with `Unsupported content type for this resource.`, and no contact form is saved.
The form tells you that kind of picture is not accepted, and keeps what you typed.
The SVG is refused too, before anything is uploaded: an SVG can carry script, and the server already refuses one as an avatar for that reason.
steps.note: Today the BMP or AVIF gives only **Unable to submit the form. Please try again.**, and the SVG is uploaded, confirmed and stored with the form (see found). The server takes JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF and SVG for this form.

steps.title: Contact form: the rate limit
do: Restart the server.
With the Network tab open, send five valid messages without photos from {page:/contact}, one after another.
Send a sixth.
Fill and send the callback form further down the page.
Restart the server and send the sixth message again.
expect: The first five each show **Form submitted successfully!**
Each answer to `create-new-contact-form` carries `RateLimit-Limit` `5`, and `RateLimit-Remaining` counts down 4, 3, 2, 1, 0.
The sixth answers 429 with the message **Too many requests**, a dash, then **please try again later.**
The page tells you that too many messages have been sent and to try again later.
The focus moves to that message.
The form keeps what you typed.
The callback form still sends: each form has its own count.
After the restart the message sends.
steps.note: Today the sixth shows only **Unable to submit the form. Please try again.** in red under the button, and the focus does not move to it (see found). The 15 minutes run from the first send and are held in the server's memory. A message with a photo uploads the photo before it is refused; the unused file is removed by the daily cleanup after 24 hours. Every accepted send emails the owner inbox.

steps.title: Callback form: what it asks
do: On {page:/contact}, scroll to **Prefer a call back?**
Open the **What is it about?** list.
Try to type 130 characters into **Full Name** and 45 into **Phone Number**.
expect: The heading **Prefer a call back?** over **Leave your name and number and we’ll ring you back, usually within one working day.**
**Full Name** and **Phone Number** side by side at desktop width, then **What is it about?**, each with a red asterisk.

The list reads **Choose a project type** until you pick, and offers seven choices in this order: **New website**, **Website redesign**, **Online shop**, **Booking system**, **SEO and performance**, **Hosting and maintenance**, **Something else**.
**Choose a project type** cannot be picked from the open list.
**Full Name** stops at 120 characters and **Phone Number** at 40.
The button reads **Request a call back**.
steps.note: The choices come from `callbackProjectTypes` in `client/src/utils/data/callbackData.js`, and the chosen text is stored as it is.

steps.title: Callback form: validation messages
do: On {page:/contact}, open the Network tab and press **Request a call back** with the callback form empty.
Type spaces into **Full Name** and `12345` into **Phone Number**, and press it again.
Fill **Full Name** properly and press it again.
Try these numbers in turn, pressing the button after each: `0784628638a`, `1234567890123456`, `+44 (0)7846 286385`.
Pick a choice from **What is it about?**
expect: Empty: **Full name is required**, **Phone number is required** and **Choose a project type** in small red text under the three boxes, each ringed in red, and the cursor in **Full Name**.
Spaces count as empty (**Full name is required**), and `12345` gives **Enter a valid phone number**.
With the name fixed, the cursor goes to **Phone Number**.
`0784628638a` (a letter) and `1234567890123456` (16 digits) give **Enter a valid phone number**; `+44 (0)7846 286385` clears it.
Picking a choice clears **Choose a project type** at once, and typing in a box clears its own message.
No request goes to `/api/contact/create-new-callback-form` while a message shows.
steps.note: A number needs 7 to 15 digits and may also use spaces, `+`, brackets, dots and hyphens. The server applies the same rule.

steps.title: Callback form: a request and its email
do: On {page:/contact}, fill **Full Name** `Callback Tester`, **Phone Number** `07700 900789`, choose **Booking system**, open the Network tab and press **Request a call back**.
In Prisma Studio, open `CallbackForm`.
Open **New Callback Request** in the owner inbox and click its footer link.
expect: While it sends, the button shows a small spinner and **Sending** with three dots.
Green text under the button: **Thanks! We’ll call you back soon.**
The boxes empty and the list goes back to **Choose a project type**.
`create-new-callback-form` answers 201.
`CallbackForm` has a row with `fullName` `Callback Tester`, `phoneNumber` `07700 900789` (spaces kept) and `projectType` `Booking system`.
The email's subject is **New Callback Request**, from **Byte Toast Studio**.

It reads **New Callback Request**, **Hi, someone has requested a callback from your website:**, then **Full Name:**, **Phone Number:** and **Project Type:** with what you entered, then **Give them a call back when you get a chance!**
The footer link **bytetoast-studio.com** opens https://bytetoast-studio.com.
steps.note: Keep this row for I12. The footer link has no `https://` today (see found). The callback form has no email box, so only the owner inbox is sent anything.

steps.title: Callback form: the rate limit
do: Restart the server.
Send five valid callback requests from {page:/contact}, then a sixth.
Send a contact form message from the same page.
expect: The first five each show **Thanks! We’ll call you back soon.**
The sixth shows, in red under the button, **Too many requests**, a dash, then **please try again later.**, and the focus moves to that message.
The boxes keep what you typed.
The contact form still sends.
steps.note: Today the focus does not move to the message (see found); a screen reader still announces it. The five rows stay for part admin-inbox to delete. Each accepted request emails the owner inbox.

steps.title: /reviews: the page and the seeded review
do: Open {page:/reviews} at desktop width, then at phone width.
Switch your system between light and dark mode.
In devtools Elements, search for `ld+json` and read each block.
expect: The tab reads **Reviews | Byte Toast Studio**.

A small eyebrow **Testimonials & Experiences** (set in capitals), the heading **Reviews for Byte Toast Studio**, and **Read real experiences, feedback, and testimonials from those who have engaged. Every review reflects authenticity, expectation, and the standard upheld.**

Under the list, a dark grey panel **Leave a Review** holds the form.
No JSON-LD block holds a `Review`, an `AggregateRating` or a `SearchAction`.
steps.note: Today the stars and **(5/5)** are white, so they vanish on the white page in light mode, and the page's JSON-LD carries a `SearchAction` for a search the site does not have (see found). The list is fetched each time the page loads, so a newly approved review shows on the next reload.

steps.title: /reviews: the form and its checks
do: On {page:/reviews}, look over the **Leave a Review** form.
Open the Network tab and press **Leave Review** with everything empty.
Type spaces into **Your Name** and **Your Review** and press it again.
Type a letter into **Your Name**.
expect: **Your Name** (red asterisk), **Title** with the hint **Optional** under it, **Rating** with five stars, and **Your Review** (red asterisk), then the button **Leave Review**.
Empty: **Please enter your name** and **Please write your review** in small red text under the two boxes, both ringed in red, and the cursor in **Your Name**.
Spaces alone count as empty, with the same two messages.
Typing in **Your Name** clears its message; the other stays.
No request goes to `/api/reviews/create-new-review` while a message shows.

steps.title: /reviews: the star rating
do: On {page:/reviews}, look at the five stars under **Rating**.
Click the third star.
Press Tab until a star has focus, then press the left and right arrow keys several times each.
Inspect the stars in devtools Elements.
expect: All five stars start filled in teal: the rating starts at 5.
Clicking the third star fills three and leaves two as grey outlines.
Tab stops once in the stars, on the chosen one.
Left and Down lower the rating one star at a time, Right and Up raise it, and it stops at 1 and at 5.
The group is labelled **Rating out of 5 stars**, each star **1 star**, **2 stars** and so on up to **5 stars**, and only the chosen star has `aria-checked` set to `true`.

steps.title: /reviews: leaving a review, which waits for approval
do: On {page:/reviews}, fill **Your Name** `Test Reviewer`, **Title** `Second test`, choose three stars and write a short review.
Open the Network tab and press **Leave Review**.
Reload the page.
In Prisma Studio, open `Review`.
In a new tab, open `http://localhost:4000/api/reviews/admin/get-all-reviews`.

The form is replaced by a blue panel: **Thank you for your review!** and **It will appear on this page once it's been reviewed by our team.**

steps.title: /reviews: no approved reviews

Tick `approved` again, save, and reload the page.

In place of the cards, a line **No reviews yet**, a dash, then **be the first to leave one below.**
The form is still there.
With `approved` ticked again, the Jamie Rivers card is back.

steps.title: /reviews: the rate limit
do: Restart the server.
Leave five reviews from {page:/reviews}, reloading the page between them to get the form back.
Leave a sixth.
expect: The first five each end on **Thank you for your review!**
The sixth answers 429, and the form says that too many reviews have been sent and to try again later.
The form keeps what you typed.
steps.note: Today the sixth shows only **Unable to submit your review. Please try again.** in red under the button (see found). The five reviews wait unapproved; part admin-inbox deletes them.

parts.part: Admin: the dashboard, forms and moderation
parts.intro: The /admin dashboard and the two inbox pages, /admin/contact-forms and /admin/callback-forms, signed in as `tom@gmail.com` (ADMIN) unless a test says otherwise. It uses the seeded rows (a contact form and a callback request from Tom Brock, an approved review and an approved public guest book message from Jamie Rivers) and the rows part forms created: the contact form with a photo (F8), the callback request (F13), the pending review (F18), the pending public and private guest book messages (F24, F25) and the one with a photo (F27). Run that part first, or create the same rows the same way. These tests approve, edit and delete rows and photos, and the last ones delete everything: reseed with `npx prisma db seed` in `server/` afterwards. Nothing here sends email. Keep a private window, signed out, open on /reviews and /guest-book: each page fetches its list when it loads, so reload it after every change to see what visitors see. Leave `FRONTEND_BUILD_HOOK_URL` empty in the server env for these tests, or every review and guest book save asks the site host for a new build. The seeded contact form's address, `tom@gmail.com`, belongs to a stranger: never send anything to it. Which roles can open these pages is covered in part admin-users.

steps.title: /admin: the dashboard
do: Sign in and open {page:/admin}.
Scroll to the bottom.
expect: The tab reads **Admin | Byte Toast Studio**.
A sky-blue band with teal lines above and below holds the heading **Admin Dashboard**.
Four sections follow, each under a blue bar with a white heading: **Manage**, **Contact Forms**, **Guest Book**, **Reviews**.
Each list shows a spinner while it loads.
There is no callback section: callback requests are only on /admin/callback-forms.
steps.note: Loading the dashboard also writes six rows to the audit log (see found, and F31).

steps.title: Quick links as an admin
do: On {page:/admin}, read the cards under **Manage**.
Click each card in turn, coming back to /admin after each.
Press Tab until a card has focus, then press Enter.
expect: Six cards in this order, each a title over a line: **Bookings** (**Requests, opening hours and closed days**), **Contact Forms** (**Messages sent from the contact page**), **Callback Requests** (**People waiting for a call back**), **Newsletter** (**Subscribers, drafts and sending**), **Blog** (**Write, edit and publish posts**), **Users** (**Roles and account status**).
There is no **Audit Log** card.
**Bookings** opens /admin/booking-admin, headed **Booking Admin**.
**Contact Forms** opens /admin/contact-forms, headed **Admin - Contact Forms**.
**Callback Requests** opens /admin/callback-forms, headed **Admin - Callback Requests**.
**Newsletter** opens /admin/newsletter-overview, headed **Newsletter**.
**Blog** opens /blog/admin, headed **Admin - Blog Posts**.
**Users** opens /admin/users, headed **User Admin**.
A card with keyboard focus shows an outline, and Enter opens it.
steps.note: What those pages do is in parts admin-booking, admin-newsletter, admin-blog and admin-users.

steps.title: Quick links as a developer
do: Open {page:/admin}.
Click **Audit Log**.
expect: Seven cards: the six from I2, then **Audit Log** (**App events, errors and triage**).
**Audit Log** opens /admin/events, headed **Audit Log**.
steps.note: Sign back in as `tom@gmail.com` for the rest of this part.

steps.title: The contact forms on the dashboard
do: On {page:/admin}, read the **Contact Forms** section.
Hover over the red circle on the Tom Brock card.
expect: The forms are listed newest first, two across on a wide screen, with the seeded Tom Brock form last.
