parts.intro: The public /booking page: the calendar, which days and times can be booked, the form and its checks, what you see after sending, the two emails, two visitors after one time, the server's own refusals, the booking limit and the time zone. Signed out unless a step says otherwise (booking works the same signed in). Reseed first with `npx prisma db seed` in `server/`, so the seeded bookings and closed day sit just ahead of today: Jamie Rivers (pending) at the first slot of the first open day at least two days ahead, Alex Morgan (confirmed) at the first slot of the next open day, Sam Taylor (cancelled) on the open day after that, and one closed day, the first Monday to Saturday at least a week ahead, with the reason `Seeded closed day (ByteToast Studio).` Look their dates up in `npx prisma studio` (tables `Booking` and `BookingClosedDay`): the tests call them Jamie's day, Alex's day, Sam's day and the seeded closed day. The seeded hours are Monday to Friday 09:00 to 17:00, Saturday 10:00 to 14:00, Sunday closed, in 60-minute slots. B11 and B15 make two real bookings with your own address, named `Test One` and `Test Two`: keep them, the admin-booking part uses them. Use addresses you can read (plus aliases such as `you+b1@gmail.com` work), never a seeded one. Booking requests are limited to 5 per 15 minutes per server process, refused ones included: B11, B15 (two) and B16 use four, and B17 restarts the server and uses up the rest on purpose. The page writes dates and times in your browser's language; the examples assume English (UK), such as `Monday, 19 October 2026` and `9:00`. The emails always write `Monday 19 October 2026` and `09:00`. Where the site's own text contains a dash, the quotes here split at it; where it ends in three dots, the quote stops before them. The time zone label assumes `SITE_TZ` is `Europe/London` or unset: it reads **British Summer Time (Europe/London)** in summer time and **Greenwich Mean Time (Europe/London)** in winter (from 25 October 2026).

steps.title: Getting to /booking, and what the page shows
do: Open {page:/} and choose **Booking** in the navbar (on a phone, open the menu first).
Go back to the home page, scroll down past the hero until the round calendar button appears fixed to the right edge of the window, and press it.
Look at {page:/booking} at desktop width and at phone width.
expect: Both routes open /booking.
The calendar button is not there on the hero itself: it appears once the sections below it are in view, and goes again if you scroll back up.
Above the heading, set in capitals: **Book an appointment**.
The heading **Booking**, then **Choose a day and time that suits you and send Byte Toast Studio a booking request. We'll check the details and email you as soon as it's confirmed.**
While the times load, a card with a spinner reads **Loading available times**.
Then three cards with round number badges 1, 2 and 3: **Choose a date**, **Choose a time** and **Your details**.
Under **Choose a time**: **Choose a date in the calendar to see the free times.**
Under **Your details**, a grey box **Your requested time** reading **No time chosen yet**, a dash, then **pick a date and a time above.**
Beside the cards on a wide screen, and below them on a phone: **How booking works**, **Opening hours** and **Prefer to talk?**.
The footer sits at the bottom and the tab reads **Booking | Byte Toast Studio**.

steps.title: How booking works, the opening hours and the contact box
do: On {page:/booking}, read the three boxes beside (or below) the calendar.
Click the phone number and the email address.
expect: **How booking works** is a numbered list: **Pick a day that suits you from the calendar.**, **Choose one of the free times on that day.**, then **Send your details**, a dash, **we’ll email you once the booking is confirmed.**
**Opening hours** lists Monday first: Monday to Friday each `9:00` to `17:00`, Saturday `10:00` to `14:00`, Sunday **Closed**.
Under the hours: **All times are British Summer Time (Europe/London).** (or Greenwich Mean Time in winter).
**Prefer to talk?** says **Call or email and we'll find a time together.** with `07846286385` and `hello@bytetoast-studio.com`.
The number opens a `tel:` link and the address a new email to `hello@bytetoast-studio.com`.

steps.title: The calendar: month, the 60-day window and moving between months
do: On {page:/booking}, look at the calendar under **Choose a date** before choosing anything.
Press the left arrow (**Previous month**).
Press the right arrow (**Next month**) until it stops.
Click a day after the last bookable one, and a day before today.
expect: It opens on the month of the first day with a free time, with no day selected.
The month name (for example **October 2026**) sits between two round arrow buttons, whose screen-reader labels are **Previous month** and **Next month**.
Under it: **Use the arrow keys to move between days and Enter to choose one.**
The columns run Monday to Sunday, headed **Mon** to **Sun**.
In the current month **Previous month** is greyed out and does nothing.
The last bookable day is today plus 60 days (opened on 18 October 2026, that is Thursday 17 December 2026). **Next month** greys out in that day's month.
Days before today and after the last day are plain grey numbers, not buttons, and clicking them does nothing.
Days with free times have a coloured border, and the legend underneath reads **Available**, **Selected** and **Closed or fully booked**.

steps.title: Closed weekdays and the seeded closed day
do: On {page:/booking}, find a Sunday inside the window.
Move to the month of the seeded closed day and find it.
Click the Sunday, then the closed day.
With a screen reader, or by inspecting the day buttons, read their labels.
expect: Every Sunday in range is grey with **Closed** under its number (the word shows from 640px wide; at phone width only the grey).
The seeded closed day is grey with **Closed** too.
Below the calendar, a box **Closed this month** lists that day in short form (for example `Mon, 26 Oct 2026`), a dash, then **Seeded closed day (ByteToast Studio).**
Clicking either selects nothing: **Choose a time** still reads **Choose a date in the calendar to see the free times.**
A Sunday is labelled like **Sunday, 25 October 2026, closed**.
The seeded day is labelled with its date followed by **closed: Seeded closed day (ByteToast Studio).**

steps.title: Today and the 12 hours' notice
do: Work out the time 12 hours from now in the site's time zone.
On {page:/booking}, look at today in the calendar.
Choose the day that 12-hours-from-now falls on, if it is open and not today.
expect: Today's number is underlined (a screen reader announces it as the current date).
Today shows **Unavailable** unless one of its slots starts at least 12 hours from now: on a weekday that only happens before 04:00, on a Saturday before 01:00. On a Sunday it shows **Closed**.
On the day the 12 hours run into, no time earlier than that moment is offered, and every later one is (apart from taken ones).
Every day after that offers its full set of times.
steps.note: The page re-checks every minute, so if you leave it open a time drops off the list within a minute of coming inside 12 hours. The server makes the same check when you send.

steps.title: Choosing a day: the 60-minute slots
do: On {page:/booking}, choose a free Monday to Friday that is not one of the seeded days.
Choose a free Saturday.
If today is before 25 October 2026, choose a free weekday after it.
expect: The chosen day takes the **Selected** colour.
**Choose a time** reads **Free times on** the date in bold, then the zone in brackets, for example **(British Summer Time (Europe/London)):**.
A weekday has 8 buttons, `9:00` to `16:00`, an hour apart. There is no `17:00`: the last slot must end by closing time.
Three buttons to a row on a phone, four on a wider screen.
`11:00` stays highlighted and **Your requested time** reads the long date, **at 11:00**, then the zone in brackets.
Choosing the Saturday clears the time (the box goes back to **No time chosen yet**) and offers 4 buttons, `10:00` to `13:00`.
For a date from 25 October 2026 onwards the zone reads **Greenwich Mean Time (Europe/London)**, because London is on GMT that day.
steps.note: Today the label is worked out for today's date and used for every date, so dates on the other side of a clock change get the wrong name (see found).

steps.title: Taken slots from the seeded bookings
do: On {page:/booking}, choose Jamie's day.
Choose Alex's day.
Choose Sam's day.
Read the screen-reader label of Jamie's day.
expect: Jamie's day has no first slot (`9:00` on a weekday, `10:00` on a Saturday). Every other time is there.
Alex's day is the same: its first slot is missing.
Sam's day still offers its first slot: a cancelled booking frees its time.
Jamie's day is labelled with its date and **7 times available** on a weekday (**3 times available** on a Saturday).

steps.title: The public data shows nothing personal about other bookings
do: Open devtools on the Network tab and reload {page:/booking}.
Click the `get-booking-data` request and open its response.
expect: It is a `GET` to `/api/bookings/get-booking-data` answering 200.

`data` holds `openingTimes` (seven rows of `dayOfWeek`, `isOpen`, `start` and `end`), `closedDays`, `takenSlots`, `slotMinutes` `60`, `windowDays` `60`, `minNoticeHours` `12`, `timezone`, `today` and `lastDate`.
`takenSlots` has two entries, Jamie's and Alex's, each with only `date` and `time`. Sam's cancelled booking is not there.
`closedDays` has the seeded day with only `date` and `reason`.
Nowhere in the response is a name, an email address, a phone number, a note, a booking id or a status.
`timezone` is the `SITE_TZ` setting (`Europe/London` when unset), `today` is today's date there, and `lastDate` is 60 days later.
steps.note: Run this before B11, or `takenSlots` also holds your own bookings (still with no names).

steps.title: Sending with nothing filled in
do: Reload {page:/booking} with the Network tab open. Without choosing a day, press **Request booking**.
Type a letter in **Full name**.
Type `Test One` in **Full name** and your address in **Email address**, still with no time chosen, and press **Request booking** again.
expect: **Full name** and **Email address** have a red asterisk. **Email address** has the hint **We’ll send your confirmation here.**, **Phone number** the hint **Optional**, and **Notes** the hint **Optional**, a dash, **anything we should know before we meet.**
After the first press: **Please enter a full name** in red under **Full name** and **Please enter an email address** under **Email address**, and both boxes get a red ring.
A red box under the cards reads **Please check the highlighted fields and try again.**
Focus moves to **Full name**.
The **Your requested time** box turns red with a red bar down its left side.
Typing in **Full name** clears its message at once.
After the second press the red box reads **Please choose a date and time before sending your request.** and focus moves to the **Your requested time** box.
No request goes to `create-new-booking` either time.

steps.title: Each field's own check
do: On {page:/booking}, choose a free day and time.
Type `A` in **Full name**, `nobody@example` in **Email address** and `12345` in **Phone number**, and press **Request booking**.
Change **Phone number** to `+44 (0)7700 900999` and press **Request booking** again.
Paste about 1,100 characters into **Notes**.
expect: **Please enter a full name** under **Full name** (one letter is too short).
**Please enter a valid email address** under **Email address**.
**Please enter a valid phone number** under **Phone number** (it takes 7 to 20 characters of digits, spaces, `+`, `(`, `)` and `-`).
Focus goes to **Full name**, the first problem, and the red box under the cards reads **Please check the highlighted fields and try again.**
On the second press `+44 (0)7700 900999` is accepted: no phone message, the other two still show.
**Notes** stops taking text at 1000 characters.
Nothing is sent.

steps.title: A successful request
do: On {page:/booking}, choose a free Monday to Friday that is not a seeded day, then `11:00`.
Fill **Full name** `Test One`, an address of yours, **Phone number** `07700 900999` and **Notes** `Testing the booking form.`
With the Network tab open, press **Request booking**.
Open the `Booking` table in Prisma Studio.
expect: The button reads **Sending request** with a spinning icon and cannot be pressed again.
The three cards give way to a panel with a green tick and the heading **Request received**, which takes focus.
Under it: **Thanks, Test One**, a dash, then **we’ll email you at** your address **once it’s confirmed.**
A grey list: **Date** with the long date, and **Time** `11:00` with the zone label under it.
**Your booking stays pending until we confirm it. Need to change something?** then the link **Get in touch**, which opens /contact.
A button **Make another booking**.
Below the panel, a green box: **Request received**, a dash, **we’ll email you once it’s confirmed.**
The request is a `POST` to `/api/bookings/create-new-booking` answering 201, with `data.booking.status` `PENDING`.
Prisma Studio has a row for Test One: status `PENDING`, that date, `11:00`, the phone and notes, and the email address in lower case.
steps.note: Sends two real emails (B12 and B13). Keep this booking: it is Test One in admin-booking. Uses 1 of the 5 booking requests.

steps.title: The customer's email
do: Open the email that arrives at the address you used in B11.
Click the footer link.
expect: Subject **Byte Toast Studio: Booking request received**, from **Byte Toast Studio**.
Heading **Booking Request Received**, then **Hi Test One,**.
**Thank you for your booking request**, a dash, **we’ve received your details and will email you as soon as it’s confirmed.**

A grey box: **Date:** written like `Monday 19 October 2026`, **Time:** `11:00` (24-hour, no time zone), **Name:** Test One, **Email:** your address, **Phone Number:** 07700 900999 and **Notes:** Testing the booking form.
Then **Need to change something? Just reply to this email.**
The footer has **Byte Toast Studio**, a link **bytetoast-studio.com** and **© 2026 Byte Toast Studio. All rights reserved.**
In development the footer link opens `http://localhost:5173`.
The server console logs a line starting `[email:booking] sent` that names `bookingRecieved` and your address.
steps.note: A reply goes to the address the mail came from (`BOOKING_ADMIN_EMAIL`), which is not the owner inbox when `BOOKING_ADMIN_RECIEVER_EMAIL` is set.

steps.title: The owner's email
do: Open the owner inbox.
Press the button in the email.
expect: Subject **New booking request: Test One,** the date and time, for example **New booking request: Test One, Monday 19 October 2026 at 11:00**.
Heading **New Booking Request**, then **Hi Byte Toast Studio,** and **You’ve received a new booking request from Test One:**
The same details box as the customer's, phone and notes included.
A green button **Review in admin** that opens `http://localhost:5173/admin/booking-admin`.
Then **The customer has been told the request is pending until you confirm or deny it.**
The same footer as B12.
steps.note: The owner inbox is `BOOKING_ADMIN_RECIEVER_EMAIL`, or `BOOKING_ADMIN_EMAIL` when that is unset.

steps.title: The time is gone afterwards, and Make another booking
do: On the success panel from B11, press **Make another booking**.
Choose Test One's day again.
In a private window open {page:/booking} and choose the same day.
Look at the `get-booking-data` response.
expect: The three cards return with the **Choose a date** heading focused, the green box gone and every field empty.
The calendar opens on the month of the first free day, with nothing selected.
Test One's day no longer offers `11:00`. Its other times are all there.
The private window does not offer `11:00` either.
`takenSlots` now includes Test One's date with `11:00`, still with no name.

steps.title: Two people after one time
do: Open {page:/booking} in this window (A) and in a private window (B).
In both, choose the same free weekday and `14:00` (not Test One's day).
In A, fill **Full name** `Test Two` and another address of yours, leave phone and notes empty, and press **Request booking**.
In B, without reloading, fill **Full name** `Test Late` and your address, and press **Request booking**.
expect: A shows **Request received**, as in B11.
B shows a red box at the top of **Choose a time**: **That time slot has just been taken**, a dash, **please pick another.**
The same words appear in the red box under the cards.
Focus moves to the **Choose a time** heading.
B's times for that day reload without `14:00`, and **Your requested time** is back to **No time chosen yet**.
B's name and email are still filled in.
B's request answered 409 in the Network tab. Prisma Studio has a `Test Two` row and no `Test Late` row.
Test Two's two emails arrive, with no **Phone Number** or **Notes** line. Nothing is sent for Test Late.
steps.note: Keep Test Two for admin-booking. Uses 2 of the 5 booking requests. The server checks the time and saves it inside one Serializable transaction, so two presses in the same instant also leave one booking; by hand you can only show them one after the other.

steps.title: A day closed while the page is open
do: In this window open {page:/booking}, choose a free weekday that is not a seeded day, choose a time, and fill `Test Closed` and your address. Do not send yet.
In a private window sign in as tom@gmail.com, open {page:/admin/booking-admin} and close that date under **Close a day**.
Back in the first window, press **Request booking**.
Reload the page and go to that day.
In the private window press **Reopen** beside that day, then reload the first window.
expect: A red box under the cards: **Bookings are closed on that day.**
No success panel, no new row in Prisma Studio and no email.
The calendar refreshes: the day turns **Closed** and the chosen time is cleared.
After the reload the day shows **Closed** and is listed under **Closed this month**.
After **Reopen** and a reload the day is bookable again.
steps.note: Today the calendar keeps offering that day and time after the refusal until you reload, and pressing again only repeats it (see found). Changing a weekday's hours under an open page fails the same way with **Choose one of the available time slots.** Uses 1 of the 5 booking requests.

steps.title: What the server refuses, and the booking limit
do: Restart the server (stop it, then `npm start` in `server/`) so the booking limit starts from zero.

On {page:/booking}, open the devtools console and paste `const send = (b) => fetch('http://localhost:4000/api/bookings/create-new-booking', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(b) }).then(async (r) => console.log(r.status, await r.json()));` (use your `VITE_API_URL` if the server is elsewhere).
Run `send({})`.
Pick a free weekday D (as `YYYY-MM-DD`) and run `send({ fullName: 'Test', email: 'nobody', date: 'D', time: '10:00' })` with D filled in.
Run it again with `email: 'test@example.com'` and `date` set to the day after `lastDate` (see B8).
Run it with `email: 'test@example.com'` and `date` a Sunday inside the window.
Run it with `email: 'test@example.com'`, `date` D and `time: '09:30'`.
Run `send({})` a sixth time.
On the page, choose a day and time, fill the form validly and press **Request booking**.
expect: 1st: `400` with the message **Name, email, date and time are required.**
2nd: `400`, **Data incorrectly formatted or malformed request**
3rd: `400`, **Choose a valid date within the booking window.**
4th: `400`, **Bookings are closed on that day.**
5th: `400`, **Choose one of the available time slots.**
6th: `429`, **Too many requests**, a dash, **please try again later.**
In the Network tab the responses carry `RateLimit-Limit: 5` and a `RateLimit-Remaining` that counts down to `0`.
On the page, the red box under the cards shows the same **Too many requests** message and no success panel.
None of this makes a booking row or sends an email.
steps.note: The limit is per form and per server process, and refused requests count. Restart the server again, or wait 15 minutes, before booking anything else.

steps.title: Using the calendar from the keyboard
do: On {page:/booking}, press Tab until a day in the calendar has focus.
Press the arrow keys, then Home, End, Page Down and Page Up.
Keep pressing Left Arrow past today, and Down Arrow past the last bookable day.
Move to a Sunday and press Enter.
Move to a free day and press Enter.
expect: The calendar is a single Tab stop: the first free day of the month (or the selected day) takes focus.
Left and Right move one day, Up and Down one week, Home and End to that week's Monday and Sunday, Page Down and Page Up one month.
The month name changes when focus crosses into another month.
Focus stops at today and at the last bookable day.
Each day is read out with its state, for example **Monday, 19 October 2026, 8 times available**.
Enter on a Sunday selects nothing.
Enter on a free day selects it and lists its times.

steps.title: The visitor's own time zone changes nothing
do: In Chrome devtools open More tools, Sensors, set Location to Other and Timezone ID to `America/Los_Angeles`, leaving Locale empty (or change your computer's time zone).
Reload {page:/booking} with devtools still open.
Choose a free weekday.
expect: The same times as before: `9:00` to `16:00` on a weekday.
The label still names Europe/London.
The underlined today is the site's date, not Los Angeles's (they differ for the first 8 hours of the UK day).
The 12 hours' notice still counts from the site's clock, as in B5.
steps.note: Turn the override off afterwards.

steps.title: The site time zone (SITE_TZ)
do: Set `SITE_TZ=America/New_York` in the server's env file and restart the server.
Reload {page:/booking} and choose a free weekday.
Set `SITE_TZ=Mars/Olympus`, restart the server and watch its console, then reload the page.
Put `SITE_TZ` back as it was and restart the server.
expect: With New York the label reads **Eastern Daylight Time (America/New York)** (**Eastern Standard Time** from 1 November 2026), and the hours box ends **All times are Eastern Daylight Time (America/New York).**
The opening hours and the times offered are the same wall-clock times, now meaning New York time.
`today` in the `get-booking-data` response is New York's date, and the 12 hours' notice counts from New York's clock.
The seeded bookings keep their stored dates and times: they do not shift.
With the invalid name the server prints `[booking] SITE_TZ is not a valid IANA timezone, using Europe/London` as it starts, and the page names Europe/London.
steps.note: Needs a server setting change and restarts. Restore it before going on.

steps.title: When the calendar cannot load
do: Stop the server and reload {page:/booking}.
Start the server again and press **Try again**.
expect: After the spinner, a card headed **Booking is unavailable right now**.
It says **We couldn't load the booking calendar (No response from the server. Please try again.). Please try again in a moment, or contact us directly to arrange a time.**
A **Try again** button under it.
The **Opening hours** box is missing; **How booking works** and **Prefer to talk?** are still there.
**Try again** loads the calendar without reloading the page.

parts.intro: /admin/booking-admin, signed in as tom@gmail.com unless a step says otherwise: the bookings list and its filters, **Confirm**, **Deny**, **Cancel booking**, **Edit**, **Delete** and **Delete all**, the opening hours, the closed days, and the emails each action sends. Run it after the booking part, or reseed and make the bookings it needs. It needs three pending bookings made on /booking with addresses you can read, named `Test One`, `Test Two` and `Test Three`: B11 and B15 made the first two; make `Test Three` the same way before you start, on a free weekday at `15:00` (restart the server first if B17 used up the booking limit). Every confirm, deny and cancel, and every edit of a pending or confirmed booking, emails the customer and the owner inbox. The seeded customers have `@example.com` addresses, so their copy never arrives (the owner's does; your sending mailbox may get a bounce). The page shows statuses as **Pending**, **Confirmed**, **Denied** and **Cancelled**; the update emails print **Awaiting confirmation** and **Confirmed**. Messages appear as toasts at the bottom of the window (bottom right on a wide screen): green ones fade after about 6 seconds, red ones stay until you press their cross (**Dismiss message**). Dates and times follow your browser's language as in the booking part; toasts and dialogs use the short form, such as `Wed, 21 Oct 2026 at 9:00`. The emails write `Wednesday 21 October 2026` and `09:00`. This part changes most booking data, the opening hours and the closed days, and ends by deleting every booking: reseed with `npx prisma db seed` afterwards.

steps.title: A USER cannot open the bookings admin
do: Sign in as user@gmail.com and open {page:/admin/booking-admin}.
Look at the navbar.
In the devtools console run `fetch('http://localhost:4000/api/bookings/get-all-bookings-admin', { credentials: 'include' }).then(async (r) => console.log(r.status, await r.json()))`.
expect: You land on the home page straight away; the bookings admin never shows.
The navbar has no **Admin** menu.
The fetch answers `403` with **This action requires an admin or developer role.**
steps.note: Signed out, the same address sends you to /login; the accounts part covers the return to the page after signing in.

steps.title: The page and the seeded bookings
do: Sign in as tom@gmail.com, open the **Admin** menu and choose **Bookings**.
Read each card.
expect: The address is /admin/booking-admin and the tab reads **Booking Admin | Byte Toast Studio**.
A banner with the heading **Booking Admin**, then three sections with coloured header bars: **Bookings** (with a red **Delete all** button), **Opening hours** and **Closed days**.
Above the list: **Status** set to **All statuses**, **Timeframe** with **Upcoming** pressed and **Past**, and **Refresh**.
**All dates and times are British Summer Time (Europe/London).** (or Greenwich Mean Time in winter).
Cards in date and time order, two columns on a wide screen, each with the name as a heading, the long date **at** the time, and a status badge.
**Jamie Rivers**: yellow **Pending**, **Email** `jamie@example.com` as a mail link, **Phone** `07700 900123`, **Notes** **First visit.**
**Alex Morgan**: green **Confirmed**, and a dash under both **Phone** and **Notes**.
**Sam Taylor**: grey **Cancelled**, **Phone** `07700 900456`, **Notes** **Can no longer make it.**
**Requested** shows when each booking was made, in your computer's time zone.

Pending cards have **Confirm** (green), **Deny** (red), **Cancel booking**, **Edit** and **Delete**. Confirmed cards have **Cancel booking**, **Edit** and **Delete**. Cancelled cards have **Edit** and **Delete**.
Test One, Test Two and Test Three show as **Pending** with your addresses.
steps.note: Every load of this list, filter change and **Refresh** writes a **Get All Requested** and a **Get All Success** row to the audit log; the admin-users part covers the log.

steps.title: Filters and Refresh
do: With the Network tab open, set **Status** to **Pending**, **Confirmed**, **Denied**, **Cancelled**, then **All statuses**.
Press **Past**, then scroll to the **Closed days** section.
Press **Upcoming**.
Press **Refresh**.
expect: **Pending** shows only pending cards, **Confirmed** only Alex Morgan, **Cancelled** only Sam Taylor.
**Denied** shows **No bookings match these filters.**
Each `get-all-bookings-admin` request carries `status=PENDING` (and so on) and `from=` today's date. **All statuses** sends no `status`.
**Past** sends `to=` yesterday's date and shows **No bookings match these filters.** (the seed has no past bookings).
With **Past** chosen, the **Closed days** list still shows the seeded closed day.
**Upcoming** brings the cards back.
**Refresh** spins its icon, shows a spinner in place of the list and reloads it.
steps.note: With **Past** chosen, the **Closed days** list currently shows **No closed days set.** (see found).

steps.title: Confirm
do: With **All statuses** and **Upcoming**, press **Confirm** on Test One.
Set **Status** to **Pending**, then back to **All statuses**.
Open {page:/booking} in another tab and choose Test One's day.
expect: No dialog: it acts at once, and the card's buttons grey out while it works.
A green toast: **Booking for Test One on** the short date **at 11:00 confirmed.**
The badge turns green **Confirmed**. **Confirm** and **Deny** go, leaving **Cancel booking**, **Edit** and **Delete**.
Under **Pending**, Test One is no longer listed.
Prisma Studio shows its status as `CONFIRMED`.
/booking still does not offer `11:00` on that day.
The toast fades after about 6 seconds, or goes at once with its cross.
steps.note: Confirm is the only status change without a dialog; **Deny**, **Cancel booking** and both deletes ask first. Sends two emails (K5).

steps.title: The confirmation emails
do: Open Test One's inbox, then the owner inbox.
expect: The customer gets **Byte Toast Studio: Your booking is confirmed**, from **Byte Toast Studio**.
It has the heading **Your Booking is Confirmed**, **Hi Test One,**, then **Great news**, a dash, **your booking has been confirmed. Here are the details:**
The details box: **Date:**, **Time:** `11:00`, **Name:**, **Email:**, **Phone Number:** and **Notes:**.
Then **If you have any questions or need to make changes, just reply to this email.** and **We look forward to seeing you!**, with no button.
The owner inbox gets **Booking confirmed: Test One,** the date, **at 11:00**.

It has the heading **Booking Confirmed**, **Hi Byte Toast Studio,**, **The following booking has been confirmed:**, the same details, **A confirmation email has been sent to the customer.** and a **Review in admin** button to /admin/booking-admin.

steps.title: A second press does nothing
do: Open {page:/admin/booking-admin} in a second tab.
In tab 1, press **Confirm** on Jamie Rivers.
In tab 2, which still shows Jamie as **Pending**, press **Confirm** on Jamie.
Still in tab 2, press **Deny** on Jamie and **Confirm** in the dialog.
Press **Refresh** in tab 2.
expect: Tab 1: a green toast **Booking for Jamie Rivers on** the short date and time **confirmed.**
Tab 2: a red toast **That action isn't allowed for the booking's current status.** that stays until you press its cross.
The **Deny** attempt gives the same red toast and changes nothing.
Both refused requests answered 409 in the Network tab.
Tab 2's card reads **Pending** until **Refresh**, then **Confirmed**.
The owner inbox gets one **Booking confirmed: Jamie Rivers,** email; the refused presses send nothing.
steps.note: Jamie's customer copy goes to `jamie@example.com` and never arrives.

steps.title: Deny, and its dialog
do: Press **Deny** on Test Two.
Press Tab several times, then **Cancel**.
Press **Deny** again and press Escape.
Press **Deny** again and **Confirm**.
Open {page:/booking} and choose Test Two's day.
expect: A dialog headed **Deny booking**: **Deny the booking request from Test Two on** the short date **at 14:00?**
A red **Cancel** button, which has focus, and a green **Confirm**.
Tab stays inside the dialog and the page behind does not scroll.
**Cancel** and Escape close it with Test Two still **Pending**, and focus goes back to **Deny**.
After **Confirm**: a green toast **Booking for Test Two on** the short date **at 14:00 denied.**
A red **Denied** badge, with only **Edit** and **Delete** left.
/booking offers `14:00` on that day again.

steps.title: The denial emails
do: Open Test Two's inbox, then the owner inbox.
Press the button in the customer's email.
expect: The customer gets **Byte Toast Studio: Update on your booking request**.
Its heading is **We’re Sorry**, a dash, **Booking Not Accepted**, then **Hi Test Two,** and **Unfortunately, we’re unable to accept your booking request for the time below:**
The details box has no **Phone Number** or **Notes** line (Test Two gave none).
Then **We apologise for any inconvenience. You’re welcome to pick another time:** and a button **Choose another time**, which opens `http://localhost:5173/booking`.
The owner gets **Booking denied: Test Two,** the date, **at 14:00**.
It has the heading **Booking Denied**, **The following booking request has been denied:**, the details, **The customer has been notified and the slot is free again.** and **Review in admin**.

steps.title: The edit form and its checks
do: Press **Edit** on Alex Morgan.
Press **Discard**.
Press **Edit** again and **Save changes** without changing anything, with the Network tab open.
Press **Edit** again. Clear **Date**, **Time** and **Full name**, type `nobody` in **Email** and `12` in **Phone**, and press **Save changes**.
Empty **Email** completely and press **Save changes**.
Press **Discard**.
expect: The card's details give way to a form: **Date**, **Time**, **Full name** and **Email** (each with a red asterisk), **Phone** and **Notes**, filled with Alex's details, and the buttons **Save changes** and **Discard**.
Focus starts in **Date**.
**Discard** closes the form unchanged and puts focus back on **Edit**.
**Save changes** with nothing changed just closes the form: no request, no toast.

In red under the fields: **Please choose a valid date**, **Please choose a valid time**, **Please enter a full name**, **Please enter a valid email address** and **Please enter a valid phone number**.
Focus moves to **Date**, the first problem.
With **Email** empty its message reads **Please enter an email address**.
Nothing is sent while a message shows, and after **Discard** Alex's booking is unchanged.

steps.title: Editing the details of a pending booking
do: Press **Edit** on Test Three, change **Notes** to `Edited by the owner.` and press **Save changes**.
Open Test Three's inbox, then the owner inbox.
expect: The button reads **Saving** while it works, then the form closes.
A green toast **Booking for Test Three updated.**
The card shows the new notes and is still **Pending**.

The customer gets **Byte Toast Studio: Your booking has been updated**, headed **Your Booking Has Been Updated**, with **Hi Test Three,** and **We’ve updated your booking. Here are the latest details:**
Its box lists **Date:**, **Time:**, **Status:** **Awaiting confirmation**, **Name:**, **Email:** and **Notes:** Edited by the owner.
There is no **Previously:** line, because the time did not change.
It ends **If anything looks wrong, just reply to this email.** and a button **View availability** to /booking.

The owner gets **Booking updated: Test Three,** the date and time, headed **Booking Updated**, with **The following booking has been updated:**, the same box, **The customer has been sent the updated details.** and **Review in admin**.

steps.title: Moving a confirmed booking to a cancelled booking's time
do: Press **Edit** on Test One, set **Date** and **Time** to Sam Taylor's (the cancelled booking) and press **Save changes**.
Open {page:/booking} and look at Test One's old day and Sam's day.
Open Test One's inbox and the owner inbox.
expect: A green toast **Booking for Test One updated.**; the card shows the new date and time and moves to its place in the list.
The move is allowed, because a cancelled booking holds no time.
/booking offers `11:00` on Test One's old day again, and no longer offers Sam's time.
The customer gets **Byte Toast Studio: Your booking has been updated** with **Previously:** the old date **at 11:00** above the new **Date:** and **Time:**, and **Status:** **Confirmed**.
The owner gets **Booking updated: Test One,** with the new date and time, and the same **Previously:** line.

steps.title: A move the server refuses
do: Press **Edit** on Test One.
Set Alex Morgan's date and time and press **Save changes**.
Set the seeded closed day at `10:00` and save; then a Sunday at `10:00`.
Set a free weekday at `09:30` and save; then the same day at `18:00`.
Set yesterday at `10:00` and save.
Press **Discard**.
expect: Alex's time: **That time slot has just been taken**, a dash, **please pick another.**
The closed day and the Sunday: **Bookings are closed on that day.**
`09:30` and `18:00`: **Choose one of the available time slots.**
Yesterday: **Choose a valid date within the booking window.**
Each message shows in red under the form and in a red toast, and the form stays open.
After **Discard**, Test One still has its K11 date and time, and no email was sent.

steps.title: Admins can go past the 60 days and inside the 12 hours
do: Edit Test One to a weekday about 70 days ahead at `10:00` and save.
If a slot later today has not started yet, edit Test One to today at that slot and save.
If a slot earlier today has passed, try today at that slot.
Edit Test One back to a free weekday inside the window and save.
expect: 70 days ahead is saved, though visitors can only book 60 days out.
Today inside the 12 hours' notice is saved too.
A time that has already passed today is refused with **Choose one of the available time slots.**
Every save sends the pair of update emails; the refusal sends none.
steps.note: Admins skip the 60-day window and the notice period, not closed days, opening hours or taken times.

steps.title: Editing a denied or cancelled booking sends nothing
do: Edit Test Two (denied): set **Notes** to `Note on a denied booking.` and save.
Edit Sam Taylor (cancelled): set **Phone** to `07700 900111` and save.
Watch the server console and both inboxes.
expect: Green toasts **Booking for Test Two updated.** and **Booking for Sam Taylor updated.**
The badges stay **Denied** and **Cancelled**.
No email reaches anyone, and the server console logs no `[email:booking]` line.

steps.title: Cancelling a pending booking, and its dialog
do: Press **Cancel booking** on Test Three.
Press **Cancel** in the dialog.
Press **Cancel booking** again and **Confirm**.
Open {page:/booking} and choose Test Three's day.
expect: A dialog headed **Cancel booking**: **Cancel the booking for Test Three on** the short date **at 15:00? Choose Confirm to cancel it or Cancel to keep it.**
**Cancel** keeps it **Pending**.
After **Confirm**: a green toast **Booking for Test Three on** the short date **at 15:00 cancelled.**
A grey **Cancelled** badge, with only **Edit** and **Delete** left.
/booking offers `15:00` on that day again.

steps.title: The cancellation emails
do: Open Test Three's inbox, then the owner inbox.
expect: The customer gets **Byte Toast Studio: Your booking has been cancelled**, headed **Your Booking Has Been Cancelled**, with **Hi Test Three,** then **We’re sorry**, a dash, **the booking below has been cancelled:**
The details box carries the notes from K10.
Then **We apologise for any inconvenience. If you’d like to rebook, choose a new time here:** and a button **Choose another time** to /booking.

The owner gets **Booking cancelled: Test Three,** the date, **at 15:00**, headed **Booking Cancelled**, with **The following booking has been cancelled:**, the details, **The customer has been notified and the slot is free again.** and **Review in admin**.

steps.title: Cancelling a confirmed booking
do: Press **Cancel booking** on Test One and **Confirm** in the dialog.
Open {page:/booking} and Test One's inbox.
expect: A green toast ending **cancelled.** and a grey **Cancelled** badge.
/booking offers Test One's time again.
The same pair of emails as K16 arrives, with Test One's details: **Byte Toast Studio: Your booking has been cancelled** and **Booking cancelled: Test One,** the date and time.

steps.title: Opening hours: the editor and its checks
do: Scroll to **Opening hours**.
Clear Monday's **Closes** and press **Save opening hours**.
Set Monday's **Closes** to `08:00` and save; then to `09:00` and save.
Set Monday back to `17:00`. Turn Sunday's **Open** switch on, leave its boxes empty, and save.
Turn Sunday off again.
expect: The editor starts **Customers can book 60-minute slots between these times. The last slot must finish by closing time.**
Seven rows, **Monday** to **Sunday**, each with an **Open** switch (screen-reader label **Open on Monday** and so on) and two time boxes, **Opens** and **Closes**.
Monday to Friday are on with `09:00` and `17:00`, Saturday on with `10:00` and `14:00`, Sunday off with empty, greyed-out boxes.
Monday with no closing time: **Enter an opening and a closing time** in red under its **Closes**, and focus moves there.
`08:00`, and `09:00` too: **Closing time must be after opening time**.
Sunday on and empty: **Enter an opening and a closing time** under its **Closes**, a red ring on its **Opens** box, and focus in **Opens**.
Changing a row clears its message.
Nothing is saved while a message shows: /booking is unchanged.

steps.title: Changing a day's hours
do: Set Monday to open `09:30` and close `12:00`, and press **Save opening hours**.
Open {page:/booking} and choose a free Monday.
Set Monday back to `09:00` and `17:00` and save.
expect: The button reads **Saving** briefly, then a green toast **Opening hours saved.**
The **Opening hours** box on /booking shows Monday `9:30` to `12:00`.
A free Monday offers only `9:30` and `10:30`: `11:30` would run past `12:00`.
After the restore, Mondays offer `9:00` to `16:00` again.
steps.note: Bookings already on a Monday keep their times.

steps.title: Closing a weekday
do: Turn Saturday's **Open** switch off and save.
Open {page:/booking}.
Turn Saturday back on and save.
expect: Saturday's boxes grey out but keep `10:00` and `14:00`.
A green toast **Opening hours saved.**
On /booking every Saturday shows **Closed**, and the hours box reads Saturday **Closed**.
Turned back on, Saturday still has `10:00` and `14:00`, and after saving Saturdays offer 4 times again.

steps.title: A fully booked day
do: Note Alex Morgan's date and time (confirmed, at that day's first slot).
Set that weekday to open at Alex's time and close one hour later, and save.

parts.intro: Everything a visitor does with the newsletter, signed out throughout: the sign-up form on /newsletter and in the home page box, the confirmation email and page, sending the link again, the unsubscribe page, and the one-click unsubscribe address that mail programs use. Every email goes through Resend, so the server needs `RESEND_API_KEY` and `EMAIL_FROM` on a domain verified in Resend; without them the forms still say they worked, but nothing arrives. Use three addresses you can read, called A, B and C below. Plus aliases of one Gmail address work (`you+nl1@gmail.com`, `you+nl2@gmail.com`, `you+nl3@gmail.com`). Never type a seeded account's address or anybody else's. Reseed (`npx prisma db seed` in `server/`) before starting: the unsubscribe tests use the seeded subscribers in `server/prisma/seed/newsletter.js` (`jamie.rivers@example.com` and `sam.patel@example.com` confirmed, `alex.morgan@example.com` pending with the confirmation token `seed-newsletter-confirmation-token`), and you copy their tokens from `npx prisma studio`, model `NewsletterSubscriber`. This part deletes and confirms subscriber rows; the admin-newsletter part starts with a reseed, which also removes A, B and C. Rate limits: the sign-up form (one counter shared by /newsletter and the home page box), the confirmation page, the resend form and the unsubscribe page each allow 5 requests per 15 minutes from your connection. They are kept in memory, so restart the server (type `rs` in the `npm run dev` terminal) where a test says so, or whenever a red message starting **Too many requests** appears. The curl commands are for Windows PowerShell: type `curl.exe`, not `curl`, which PowerShell turns into Invoke-WebRequest. In the Network tab each POST is preceded by an OPTIONS preflight: ignore it. Email links point at `http://localhost:5173` because `NODE_ENV` is not `production`.

steps.title: /newsletter: what the page shows

expect: /newsletter opens.

At the top: **Stay in the loop** in small capitals, the heading **Newsletter**, and **News, updates and the occasional offer from Byte Toast Studio, straight to your inbox. No spam, and you can unsubscribe at any time with the link in every email.**

It has **Name** (placeholder `Your name`, with **Optional** in small text under the box) and **Email** with a red asterisk (placeholder `you@example.com`).
The two fields sit side by side at desktop width and one above the other at phone width.
Under them one button, **Subscribe**.

The second card is headed **Didn't get the confirmation email?** with **Check your spam folder first. Confirmation links expire after 24 hours**, a dash, then **enter your email below and we'll send a fresh one.**

steps.title: Sign up with your own address

steps.title: The confirmation email
do: Open the email that arrives at address A. Do not press its button yet.
Compare the link printed under the button with `confirmationToken` in Prisma Studio.

The heading inside the email repeats the subject.

steps.title: /newsletter/sign-up-success: a good link confirms

Refresh address A's row in Prisma Studio.
Press **Go to Home**.

Then the heading becomes **Subscription Confirmed** with **You're subscribed**, a dash, then **thanks for signing up! Look out for our next newsletter in your inbox.**

steps.title: An expired link

steps.title: Resend: checks made in the browser

Type `bad` and press it.

`bad`: **Enter a valid email address**.

steps.title: The sign-up box on the home page, and none in the footer
do: Open {page:/} and scroll to the end of the page, just above the footer.
Press **Subscribe** with the fields empty.
Type `Third` in **Name** and address C in **Email**, and press **Subscribe**.
Scroll to the footer, then open {page:/about} and {page:/contact} and look at their footers.
expect: The last section before the footer, after the call to action, has **Stay in the loop** in small capitals and the heading **Subscribe to our newsletter**.

**Byte Toast Studio: Confirm your newsletter subscription** arrives at C, greeting **Hello Third,**
A row for C appears in Prisma Studio with `confirmed` `false`.

steps.title: /newsletter/unsubscribe waits for a button press
do: In Prisma Studio, copy the `unsubscribeToken` of `jamie.rivers@example.com`.
With the Network tab open, go to `http://localhost:5173/newsletter/unsubscribe?token=` followed by that token.
Reload the page once.
Refresh Prisma Studio.
expect: The heading is **Unsubscribe**.
It says **Click the button below to stop receiving the Byte Toast Studio newsletter. Your email address will be removed from our list.**
Below it an **Unsubscribe** button and a **Go to Home** link.

Jamie Rivers is still in Prisma Studio.
The tab reads **Unsubscribe | Byte Toast Studio**.

steps.title: Unsubscribing
do: On the same page, press **Unsubscribe**.
Refresh Prisma Studio.
expect: While it works the button reads **Unsubscribing** with an ellipsis.
The heading becomes **You've Been Unsubscribed**.
The message is **You've been unsubscribed and won't receive any more newsletters from us.**
The explanation and the **Unsubscribe** button are gone; **Go to Home** stays.

Go to {page:/newsletter/unsubscribe?token=not-a-real-token} and press **Unsubscribe**.

Press **Contact us**.

There is no **Unsubscribe** button and no request is made.
Two links: **Contact us** and **Go to Home**.
**Contact us** opens /contact.

steps.title: One-click unsubscribe: the POST that mail programs send
do: In Prisma Studio, copy the `unsubscribeToken` of `sam.patel@example.com`.
In Windows PowerShell run `curl.exe -i -X POST "http://localhost:4000/api/newsletter/one-click-unsubscribe?token=TOKEN" -d "List-Unsubscribe=One-Click"` with the copied token in place of `TOKEN`.
Refresh Prisma Studio.
Run the same command again.
Run it with no token: `curl.exe -i -X POST "http://localhost:4000/api/newsletter/one-click-unsubscribe" -d "List-Unsubscribe=One-Click"`.
expect: The first run answers `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` with `{"status":"success","message":"You've been unsubscribed and won't receive any more newsletters from us."}`.
Its headers include `RateLimit-Limit: 300`: only the site-wide limit applies here, not the forms' 5 per 15 minutes.
Sam Patel's row is gone from Prisma Studio.
The second run answers `404` with `That unsubscribe link is invalid or has already been used.`
With no token it answers `400` with `Data incorrectly formatted or malformed request`.
steps.note: This is what a mail program's own Unsubscribe button does with the address in an issue's `List-Unsubscribe` header (admin-newsletter part). No page and no press are involved.

steps.title: One-click address opened in a browser goes to the page with the button
do: In Prisma Studio, copy the `unsubscribeToken` of `alex.morgan@example.com`.
Run `curl.exe -i "http://localhost:4000/api/newsletter/one-click-unsubscribe?token=TOKEN"` with that token.
Run `curl.exe -i "http://localhost:4000/api/newsletter/one-click-unsubscribe"`.
Paste the first address, with the token, into the browser's address bar.
Without pressing anything on the page, refresh Prisma Studio.
expect: The first run answers `HTTP/1.1 302 Found` with `Location: http://localhost:5173/newsletter/unsubscribe?token=` and the same token.
With no token, `Location` is `http://localhost:5173/newsletter/unsubscribe`.
The browser lands on the **Unsubscribe** page with its **Unsubscribe** button.

steps.note: With `NODE_ENV=production` the redirect goes to `https://bytetoast-studio.com`.

steps.title: Sign-up limit: 5 per 15 minutes
do: Restart the server.
On {page:/newsletter}, subscribe address A (confirmed, so nothing is emailed). Reload and repeat until you have pressed **Subscribe** six times.
After the sixth, run `document.activeElement` in the devtools console.
Open {page:/} and subscribe address A in the home page box.
expect: Presses one to five each answer **You're already subscribed**, a dash, then **thanks for being here!**
The sixth shows in red under the **Subscribe** button: **Too many requests**, a dash, then **please try again later.**
The form and the address you typed stay on screen.
Focus has moved to the red message: the console prints its `div`.
The home page box answers with the same red message: both use one counter.
steps.note: Counted per connection and kept in memory: restarting the server clears it. The focus check fails at present (see found).

steps.title: Resend limit: 5 per 15 minutes
do: On {page:/newsletter}, press **Resend confirmation email** six times with `nobody-here@example.com`, typing it again each time (the field empties after each reply).
expect: Presses one to five each show **If that email is waiting to be confirmed, we've sent a new confirmation link.**, although the sign-up form is at its limit from N22.
The sixth shows in red under the button: **Too many requests**, a dash, then **please try again later.**
No email is sent at any point.
steps.note: Focus does not move to the red message here either (see found).

steps.title: Unsubscribe limit: 5 per 15 minutes
do: Go to {page:/newsletter/unsubscribe?token=not-a-real-token} and press **Unsubscribe** six times.
expect: Presses one to five each show **Unsubscribe Failed** and the red **That unsubscribe link is invalid or has already been used.**
The sixth shows the red **Too many requests** message, ending **please try again later.**
The **Unsubscribe** button is still there afterwards.

steps.title: Confirmation page limit: 5 per 15 minutes
do: With the Network tab open, go to {page:/newsletter/sign-up-success?token=not-a-real-token} and reload it five times (six opens in all).
expect: Opens one to five show **Confirmation Failed** and the red **This confirmation link is invalid, has expired or has already been used.**
On the sixth, the `confirm-email` request answers `429`.
The sixth page says there have been too many tries and to wait, instead of calling the link invalid.
steps.note: The last check fails at present: the page shows the invalid-link message for any failure, so a good link opened a sixth time in 15 minutes, or opened while the server is down, is called dead too (see found).

steps.title: The server checks the forms too
do: Restart the server.
Run `curl.exe -i -X POST http://localhost:4000/api/newsletter/subscribe-to-newsletter -d "email=not-an-email"`.
Run `curl.exe -i -X POST http://localhost:4000/api/newsletter/resend-verification-email -d "email=not-an-email"`.
Run `curl.exe -i -X POST http://localhost:4000/api/newsletter/confirm-email -d "token="`.
Run `curl.exe -i -X POST http://localhost:4000/api/newsletter/unsubscribe -d "token="`.
expect: All four answer `400` with `{"status":"fail","message":"Data incorrectly formatted or malformed request"}`.
Each carries `RateLimit-Limit: 5`, the per-form limit.
No row is added to `NewsletterSubscriber`.
steps.note: The browser forms stop these before sending, so only a direct request reaches the server's own check. Each counts towards that form's 5.

steps.title: The Resend webhook refuses an unsigned post
do: In `server/`, run `npm run env:check` to see whether `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is empty.
Run `curl.exe -i -X POST http://localhost:4000/api/newsletter/resend-webhook -d "{}"`.
Look at the `NewsletterSubscriber` rows.
expect: With the secret empty it answers `503` with `{"status":"error","message":"RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set."}`; with it set, `401` with `{"status":"fail","message":"Webhook signature could not be verified."}`.
There is no `RateLimit-Limit` header: the webhook sits in front of the site-wide limit.
No subscriber is removed.
steps.note: Resend posts here after a hard bounce, a spam complaint or a suppression, and a correctly signed event deletes that address; a passing bounce leaves it. Resend can only reach a public address, so the full round trip is checked on a deployed API with Resend's test events (`LAUNCH-CHECKLIST.md`).

parts.intro: The /admin/newsletter-overview page: the subscriber list, drafts, publishing and the sent issues, and the email an issue becomes. Signed in as `tom@gmail.com` (`ADMIN`) unless a test says otherwise; `dev@gmail.com` gets the same page. Reseed first (`npx prisma db seed` in `server/`), which also removes the addresses used in the newsletter part. The seed (`server/prisma/seed/newsletter.js`) gives two confirmed subscribers, `jamie.rivers@example.com` and `sam.patel@example.com`, one pending, `alex.morgan@example.com`, the draft **Coming soon: our spring update** and the sent issue **Welcome to the newsletter**. **Publishing really emails every confirmed subscriber through Resend**, at once and with no undo. The seeded addresses are on example.com, a reserved domain nobody owns, so they are not anybody's inbox, but Resend would still try to deliver to them and the failures count against your sending domain. So L5 and L6 delete every seeded subscriber, and L7 signs up addresses of your own, before anything is published. Never publish while an address you do not control is confirmed. Sending needs `RESEND_API_KEY` and `EMAIL_FROM` on a domain verified in Resend. You need three addresses you can read, called D, E and G below (plus aliases such as `you+issue1@gmail.com` work). Look at the data in `npx prisma studio`, models `NewsletterSubscriber` and `Newsletter`. Reseed when you are done; until then D and G stay subscribed.

steps.title: The page opens for an admin
do: Sign in as `tom@gmail.com`.
Open the navbar's **Admin** menu and choose **Newsletter**.
Also open {page:/admin/newsletter-overview} directly.
expect: A band at the top with the heading **Newsletter** and **Subscribers, drafts and sending**.
Three sections, each under a bar: **Subscribers** (buttons **Refresh** and **Delete all**), **Drafts** (button **New draft**) and **Sent issues** (button **Refresh**).
Each section shows a spinner until its list has loaded.
The tab reads **Newsletter Admin | Byte Toast Studio**.
steps.note: The **Newsletter** quick link on /admin opens the same page (admin-inbox part).

steps.title: Subscribers: the seeded list
do: Look at **Subscribers**.
With devtools on the Network tab, press **Refresh** and open the `get-subscriber-list` response.
expect: Three tiles: **Total** 3, **Confirmed** 2, **Pending** 1.
A table with the columns **Name**, **Email**, **Status** and **Joined**.

parts.intro: What a visitor sees of the blog: the /blog list (its cards, paging, thumbnails and the empty state), a published post at `/blog/<slug>` (title, subtitle, author, dates, every kind of content block, tags, the breadcrumb, the head tags and the JSON-LD), a missing post, drafts hidden from visitors and from a USER but open to an admin, filtering by tag through the API, and how the browser's blog cache picks up a change made in admin. Start from a fresh seed (`npx prisma db seed` in `server/`). The seed has two posts: `welcome-to-the-blog`, published, by Admin, tags Announcement and News, holding a paragraph, a heading, a list and an internal link, and `draft-post`, a draft with no description. Most tests are signed out. G11 and G13 create posts as tom@gmail.com, and G20 to G22 change the seeded post, so reseed when this part is done and before the next one. Uploads in G11 need the server's `STORAGE_*` settings, bucket CORS that allows http://localhost:5173, and `VITE_MEDIA_CDN` in the client env (without it every uploaded file's address is `#` and shows broken). Dates follow your browser's language settings: the examples assume a UK browser. Read head tags in devtools Elements under `<head>`; the JSON-LD scripts sit in the page body. Nothing in this part sends email.

steps.title: /blog: the page and the seeded post
do: Open {page:/blog}.
Look at the tab title and the headings.
Scroll to the end of the list.
expect: The tab reads **Blog | Byte Toast Studio**.
At the top, centred: the heading **Byte Toast Studio Blog** and under it **Guides, studio news and the stories behind our projects.**
Above the cards: **Latest Articles**, then **The newest posts first**, then a rule.
**Loading** and a spinner show for a moment, then a single card: **Welcome to the blog**.
**Draft post** is not on the list.
Under the card: **Page 1 of 1**, with no **Previous** and no **Next** button.
steps.note: The list page's own head tags and JSON-LD are checked in the cross-cutting part.

steps.title: A card on the list
do: On {page:/blog}, look at the **Welcome to the blog** card at phone width, then wider than 1024px.
Hover over the card.
Click the card away from its button.
Go back and press **Read More**.
expect: The card shows the title **Welcome to the blog** and the subtitle **First post (ByteToast Studio seed).**
Its text is the first paragraph: **Test blog seed post (ByteToast Studio).**
There is no picture: the seeded post has no thumbnail.
Under **Read More** the byline reads **By Admin**, a `|`, then the publish date written out (for example `18 October 2026`).
Hovering shows the tooltip **Read more about Welcome to the blog**.
Clicking the card scrolls to the top and, after a short pause, opens /blog/welcome-to-the-blog.
**Read More** does the same.
Cards run one to a row on a phone, two from 768px wide and three from 1280px.

steps.title: A card at tablet width
do: Make the window between 768 and 1023 pixels wide and open {page:/blog}.
expect: The card switches to its tablet layout: title, subtitle, text, **Read More** and the byline in one column (a thumbnail, when there is one, goes on the right).
The byline still separates the name from the date, as at the other widths: **By Admin**, a `|`, then the date.
steps.note: At this width it currently reads `By Admin18 October 2026`, run together (see found).

steps.title: The empty list
do: In `server/`, run `npx prisma studio`, open BlogPost and set `isPublished` to `false` on the `welcome-to-the-blog` row. Save.
Reload {page:/blog}.
Set `isPublished` back to `true`, save, and reload /blog.
expect: Where the cards were, centred: **No posts available**.
Below it **Page 1 of 1**, with no **Previous** and no **Next**.
After setting it back, the card returns.
steps.note: Editing the row in Prisma Studio leaves `publishedAt` alone, so the post keeps its date. The editor's way to do this (unpublishing) is in part Admin: the blog.

steps.title: The list and a post when the API is down
do: Stop the server (Ctrl+C in its terminal).
Open {page:/blog} in a new tab.
Open {page:/blog/welcome-to-the-blog} in another new tab and look at its robots tag.
Start the server again (`npm start`). In the /blog tab click **Home** in the bar, then **Blog**.
expect: /blog says the posts could not be loaded, instead of claiming there are none.
The post page says the post could not be loaded, instead of **Post not found**.
The post page's robots tag stays `index,follow`: a real post is never marked `noindex` because the API failed.
With the server back, returning to /blog shows the post.
steps.note: Today the list shows **No posts available** and keeps showing it for up to a minute after the server is back, and the post shows **Post not found** and **Blog post not found.** with `noindex,follow` (see found).

steps.title: A published post: heading, byline and blocks
do: Open {page:/blog/welcome-to-the-blog}.
Hover over **Get in touch**, then click it with devtools Network open.
Go back.
expect: A box reading **Loading** shows for a moment, then the post in a card in the middle of the page.
Heading **Welcome to the blog**, and under it **First post (ByteToast Studio seed).**
A line with **By Admin** on the left and the publish date on the right, in the short style (for example `18/10/2026`).
Then, in order: the paragraph **Test blog seed post (ByteToast Studio).**, the heading **What to expect**, a bulleted list **News**, **Updates**, **Behind the scenes**, and the link **Get in touch**.
Hovering **Get in touch** shows the tooltip **Get in touch**, and in devtools its `aria-label` is `Navigate to Get in touch`.
**Get in touch** opens /contact without reloading the page (no document request in Network).
There is no **EDIT** link while signed out.
The tab reads **Welcome to the blog | Byte Toast Studio**.

steps.title: Tags on a post
do: On {page:/blog/welcome-to-the-blog}, scroll to the bottom of the post card.
Click one of the tags.
Look at the cards on {page:/blog}.
expect: A heading **Tags:** and two rounded chips, **Announcement** and **News**, in alphabetical order.
The chips are plain labels: clicking one does nothing.
The cards on /blog show no tags.

steps.title: The breadcrumb and its BreadcrumbList
do: On {page:/blog/welcome-to-the-blog}, look above the post card.
Click **Blog**, go back, then click **Home**.
Go back. In devtools Elements, search the page for `BreadcrumbList`.
Open {page:/blog} and search for `BreadcrumbList` again.
expect: A trail **Home** / **Blog** / **Welcome to the blog**, with a `/` between the names.
**Home** and **Blog** are underlined links to / and /blog.
**Welcome to the blog** is plain text with `aria-current` set to `page`.
The trail is a `nav` element labelled `Breadcrumb`.
One `application/ld+json` script holds a `BreadcrumbList` with three `ListItem` entries at positions 1, 2 and 3, named `Home`, `Blog` and `Welcome to the blog`.
Their `item` values are `https://bytetoast-studio.com/`, `https://bytetoast-studio.com/blog` and `https://bytetoast-studio.com/blog/welcome-to-the-blog`.
/blog itself has no trail and no BreadcrumbList.

steps.title: The post's head tags
do: Open {page:/blog/welcome-to-the-blog} and expand `<head>` in devtools Elements.
In Prisma Studio, look at the post's `publishedAt` and `updatedAt`.
expect: `<title>` is `Welcome to the blog | Byte Toast Studio`.
The `description` meta is the post's description field: `The first post on the ByteToast Studio blog: what we will write about, how often new posts go up, and where to send questions or ideas.`
The `robots` meta is `index,follow`.
The canonical link is `https://bytetoast-studio.com/blog/welcome-to-the-blog`.
`og:type` is `article`.
`og:title` is `Welcome to the blog` and `og:description` is the same text as the description.
`og:url` is the canonical address.
`og:image` and `twitter:image` are `https://bytetoast-studio.com/brand/og-default.jpg`, because the post has no thumbnail.
`twitter:card` is `summary_large_image`.
`article:published_time` is the post's `publishedAt` and `article:modified_time` its `updatedAt`, both as ISO strings ending in `Z`.
steps.note: These are the tags the browser builds. What a crawler gets without JavaScript (the pre-rendered page) is checked in the cross-cutting part.

steps.title: The post's BlogPosting JSON-LD
do: On {page:/blog/welcome-to-the-blog}, search devtools Elements for `BlogPosting` and read that script.
expect: An `application/ld+json` script in the body with `@type` `BlogPosting` and `headline` `Welcome to the blog`.
`description` matches the description meta.
`datePublished` and `dateModified` are the same ISO strings as `article:published_time` and `article:modified_time`.
`author` is a `Person` named `Admin`.
`image` is `https://bytetoast-studio.com/brand/og-default.jpg`.
`mainEntityOfPage` is a `WebPage` with `@id` `https://bytetoast-studio.com/blog/welcome-to-the-blog`.
`publisher` is the `Organization` `Byte Toast Studio`, `@id` `https://bytetoast-studio.com/#org`, with the logo `https://bytetoast-studio.com/brand/logo.png`.

steps.title: Images, video and an external link in a post
do: Sign in as tom@gmail.com and open {page:/blog/create-new-post}.

Type `Media test` in **Title** and press Tab. Type `Images, video and links` in **Subtitle**, `Media, Test` in **Tags (comma-separated)**, and in **Meta description** `This test post checks the blog editor on the Byte Toast Studio starter: content blocks, tags, uploads and publish rules.` Leave **Author Name** empty and **Publish now (untick to save as a draft)** ticked.
Press **Add Paragraph** and type `A paragraph above the media.`
Press **Add Image**, choose a JPEG or PNG under 5MB and tick **Use as thumbnail**.
Press **Add Video** and choose an MP4 under 20MB.
Press **Add Link**, type `Example site`, choose **External** and type `https://example.com`.
Press **Submit Post** and wait for **Created blog post: Media test**.
Log out, open {page:/blog/media-test} and play the video.
Click **Example site**.
expect: The post shows, in order: the paragraph, the image, the video and the link.
The image loads from your `VITE_MEDIA_CDN` host, with the alt text **Image from Media test** and no caption.
The video has the browser's controls and plays.
**Example site** opens https://example.com in a new tab.
In devtools the link has `target` `_blank`, `rel` `noopener noreferrer`, the title **Example site** and the `aria-label` `Opens external link: Example site (new tab)`.
There is no **By** name, because **Author Name** was left empty; the date still shows on the right.
In the `BlogPosting` JSON-LD, `author` is the `Organization` `Byte Toast Studio` (`@id` `https://bytetoast-studio.com/#org`), not a `Person`.
The tags read **Media** and **Test**.
steps.note: Creates a post and two uploads: reseed when the part is done. The editor itself is tested in part Admin: the blog.

steps.title: Thumbnails on the list and in link previews
do: Signed out, with **Media test** from G11 published, open {page:/blog}.
Open {page:/blog/media-test} and expand `<head>`.
expect: **Media test** is the first card and shows the image chosen as thumbnail, with the alt text **Media test thumbnail**.
Its text is **A paragraph above the media.** and there is no **By** name.
Its byline is just the date, with no stray `|` in front of it.
**Welcome to the blog** still has no picture.
On the post, `og:image` and `twitter:image` are the thumbnail's address on your `VITE_MEDIA_CDN` host.
The JSON-LD `image` is the same address.
steps.note: Without `VITE_MEDIA_CDN` the thumbnail's address is `#` and the card shows a broken image. The byline currently starts with a stray `|` at phone and desktop widths (see found).

steps.title: Paging, and the cut-off card text
do: Sign in as tom@gmail.com and open {page:/blog/create-new-post}.

Make 9 published posts. For each: type `Paging test 1` (then 2, 3 and so on to 9) in **Title** and press Tab so **Slug** fills in; put `Paging test post for the Byte Toast Studio blog list. It only exists to fill a second page of nine posts and can be deleted once the test is done.` in **Meta description**; add one paragraph `This first paragraph is deliberately longer than one hundred characters, so the card on the blog list has to cut it short and add an ellipsis.`; press **Submit Post**. Before the next one, clear **Slug**, change **Title** and press Tab.
Log out and open {page:/blog}.
Press **Next**, then **Previous**.
Click **Home** in the bar, then **Blog**.
expect: Page 1 shows 9 cards, newest first: **Paging test 9** at the top down to **Paging test 1**.
Each paging card's text is the paragraph's first 100 characters, ending `so the card on the blog lis`, followed by an ellipsis character.
Under the cards: **Page 1 of 2**, a **Next** button on the right and no **Previous**.
**Next** shows **Loading** and a spinner, then page 2 with the older posts, ending with **Welcome to the blog**.
Page 2 reads **Page 2 of 2**, with **Previous** on the left and no **Next**.
**Previous** brings page 1 back at once, with no loading.
Leaving /blog and coming back starts again at page 1.
steps.note: Creates 9 posts: reseed when the part is done. The posts may share one description: nothing compares posts with each other. With G11's post there are 11 published posts, so page 2 holds two.

steps.title: Filtering by tag (API only)
do: Open `http://localhost:4000/api/blog/get-blog-posts-by-tag/News` in the browser.
Open the same address ending `/news`.
Open the one ending `/Media`.
Open `http://localhost:4000/api/blog/get-blog-posts-by-tag/News?page=2`.
