parts.intro: The blog editor for ADMIN and DEVELOPER: the list at /blog/admin, the form at /blog/create-new-post, editing at `/blog/edit/<postId>`, the publish rules and their exact messages, uploads, deleting, and the frontend rebuild hook (`FRONTEND_BUILD_HOOK_URL`). Start from a fresh seed (`npx prisma db seed` in `server/`) and sign in as tom@gmail.com (ADMIN) unless a test says otherwise; dev@gmail.com (DEVELOPER) can do all the same. Every test changes the blog: reseed when the part is done. Later tests use posts made earlier: **Image check** (E18) in E31, **Video check** (E19) and **Tag check** (E16) in E36. Uploads need `STORAGE_*` in the server env, bucket CORS that allows http://localhost:5173, and `VITE_MEDIA_CDN` in the client env so previews show. Each file makes two calls (presign and confirm) against a limit of 20 per 15 minutes, so about ten files per 15 minutes; past that, the form shows **Too many requests** followed by a dash and **please try again later.** Restarting the server clears it. The create and edit forms keep unsaved work in local storage (`createBlogPostDraft:v1` and `editBlogPostDraft:v2:<postId>`). To look at rows, run `npx prisma studio` in `server/`: BlogPost, BlogTag, BlogPostMedia, MediaItem and AppEvent. Three descriptions are used throughout: the 120-character `This test post checks the blog editor on the Byte Toast Studio starter: content blocks, tags, uploads and publish rules.`, the 156-character `This test post checks the blog editor on the Byte Toast Studio starter site: its content blocks, tags, image and video uploads and the rules for publishing.`, and `Too short.` Blog changes send no email.

steps.title: A USER cannot open the editor pages
do: In Prisma Studio, copy the `id` of **Welcome to the blog** from BlogPost.
Sign in as user@gmail.com.
Type {page:/blog/admin} into the address bar.
Then {page:/blog/create-new-post}.
Then `/blog/edit/<id>` with the id you copied.
expect: Each address sends you to the home page.
No message is shown and none of the editor pages appears, beyond a brief spinner.
steps.note: The admin menu for each role is covered in the admin-users part.

steps.title: Signed out: sent to sign in, then back
do: Signed out, open {page:/blog/create-new-post}.
Sign in as tom@gmail.com on the page you land on.
expect: You land on /login.
After signing in you are taken back to /blog/create-new-post, not to the home page.

steps.title: The API refuses a USER and a visitor
do: Signed in as user@gmail.com, open `http://localhost:4000/api/blog/get-blog-posts-by-id/<id>` with the id of **Welcome to the blog**.
Log out and open the same address.
expect: As user@gmail.com the answer is 403 with the message `This action requires an admin or developer role.`
Signed out it is 401 with the message `No valid session found.`
steps.note: Creating, updating and deleting sit behind the same two checks.

steps.title: /blog/admin: the list of posts
do: Sign in as tom@gmail.com, open the **Admin** menu in the bar and choose **Blog Admin**.
Hover over **Edit** and **Delete** on a row.
Press **Create New Blog +**, then go back.
Press **Edit** on **Draft post**, then go back.
expect: The tab reads **Blog Admin | Byte Toast Studio**.
A header **Admin - Blog Posts**, with **Create, edit and review you current blog** under it.
A button **Create New Blog +**, then the heading **Summary of blogs**.
Five empty bars show while it loads, then one row per post, drafts included, newest created first: **Draft post**, then **Welcome to the blog**.
**Draft post** has an amber dot, **Draft** and **Created** with its creation date.
**Welcome to the blog** has a green dot, **Published** and its publish date.
From 640px wide the same date also shows at the right of the row, before the buttons.
Each row has a green **Edit** and a red **Delete**, with tooltips such as **Edit Draft post** and **Delete Draft post**.
**Create New Blog +** opens /blog/create-new-post.
**Edit** opens `/blog/edit/<id>` for that row's post.
Dates are in the short style (for example `18/10/2026`).
steps.note: With no posts at all the list reads **No blog posts yet.**

steps.title: /blog/create-new-post: what the form shows
do: Open {page:/blog/create-new-post}.
expect: The tab reads **Create Blog Post | Byte Toast Studio** and the `robots` meta is `noindex,nofollow`.

The header reads **Create Blog Post**, **Create a new blog post by adding text, images or video in the order you want them displayed**, then in bold **Be sure to set a image as thumbnail image using the checkbox!**
The form is headed **Create Blog Post** and has boxes with the placeholders **Title**, **Slug** and **Subtitle**.

Next is the labelled box **Meta description**, with the placeholder **One or two whole sentences on what the post answers, in the words people search for.** and under it **0 of 120 to 156 characters. Needed to publish.**
Then boxes with the placeholders **Subject**, **Location**, **Author Name** and **Tags (comma-separated)**.
**Author Name** is empty: it is not filled from your account.
The tick box **Publish now (untick to save as a draft)** is ticked.
**Content Sections** with six buttons: **Add Paragraph**, **Add Image**, **Add Video**, **Add Heading**, **Add List** and **Add Link**.
**Submit Post** at the bottom, and no autosave banner while the form is empty.
steps.note: If an earlier visit left work in local storage the form opens with it: press **Click to discard draft** first.

steps.title: The slug: from the title, and as the server keeps it
do: On {page:/blog/create-new-post}, type `Café au lait & croissants` in **Title** and press Tab.
Change the title to `Something else` and press Tab.
Clear **Slug**, click into **Title** and press Tab.
Change **Title** to `Slug check`, type `My First Post!` in **Slug**, untick **Publish now** and press **Submit Post**.
Open {page:/blog/my-first-post}.
expect: **Slug** fills with `caf-au-lait-croissants`: letters outside a to z are dropped rather than turned into plain letters, and each run of other characters becomes one `-`.
Changing the title later leaves the slug as it was.
With **Slug** empty, leaving **Title** fills it again from the current title: `something-else`.
The post saves (**Created blog post: Slug check**) under the slug `my-first-post`: the server lower-cases the typed slug and turns the spaces and `!` into dashes the same way.
/blog/my-first-post opens the draft for you as an admin.

steps.title: A slug that is one of the editor's own addresses
do: On {page:/blog/create-new-post}, type `Admin` in **Title**, press Tab, untick **Publish now** and press **Submit Post**.
Open {page:/blog/admin}.
Delete the **Admin** post from the list if it was saved.
expect: The editor refuses the slug `admin`, because /blog/admin is the editor's own page, and asks for another one.
No post is saved at an address that can never open it.
steps.note: Today the post saves as `admin` and /blog/admin keeps showing the post list, so the post can never be opened. `create-new-post` behaves the same (see found).

steps.title: A title and a slug are required
do: On {page:/blog/create-new-post}, with devtools Network open, press **Submit Post** with everything empty.
Type `Required check` in **Title**, press Tab, clear **Slug** and press **Submit Post**.
Type `!!!` in **Slug** and press **Submit Post**.
expect: Both first presses show **Please provide both a title and a slug.** in bold red, in a box at the top of the form.
Neither of them sends a request.
With `!!!` the server answers **A blog post needs a title and slug.** in the same box.
No post is created.

steps.title: The meta description counter
do: On {page:/blog/create-new-post}, type `Too short.` in **Meta description**.
Replace it with the 120-character description.
Replace it with the 157-character `This test post checks the blog editor on the Byte Toast Studio starter site: its content blocks, tags, image and video uploads, and its rules for publishing.`
Add three spaces to the end of it.
Paste a text of about 400 characters.
expect: With `Too short.` the line reads **10 of 120 to 156 characters. Needed to publish.** in bold red, and the box has a red ring.
With the 120-character text it reads **120 of 120 to 156 characters. Needed to publish.** in normal type, and the ring goes.
With the 157-character text it reads **157 of 120 to 156 characters. Needed to publish.** in bold red.
Spaces at the ends are not counted: the number stays at 157.
The box stops taking text at 300 characters.

steps.title: Publishing without a good description is refused
do: On {page:/blog/create-new-post}, type `Publish rules` in **Title** and press Tab. Leave **Meta description** empty and **Publish now** ticked, and press **Submit Post**.
Put the 119-character `This test post checks the blog editor on the Byte Toast Studio starter: content blocks, tags, uploads and publish rule.` in **Meta description** and press **Submit Post**.
Put in the 157-character text from E9 and press **Submit Post**.
expect: While each request runs the button reads **Submitting**, with an ellipsis.
Empty: **Add a meta description (120 to 156 characters) before publishing.** in bold red at the top of the form, and the page scrolls up to it.
119 characters: **The meta description must be 120 to 156 characters.**
157 characters: **The meta description must be 120 to 156 characters.** again.
No post is created: /blog/admin has no **Publish rules** row.

steps.title: Publishing with 120 and with 156 characters
do: Carry on from E10: put the 120-character description in **Meta description**, add a paragraph `Hello.` and press **Submit Post**.
Change **Title** to `Publish rules 156` and **Slug** to `publish-rules-156`, put the 156-character description in **Meta description** and press **Submit Post**.
Reload the page.
Open {page:/blog/admin} and {page:/blog}, then look at the two rows in BlogPost and at AppEvent in Prisma Studio.
expect: The first save shows **Created blog post: Publish rules** in green at the top of the form, and the autosave banner goes.
The second shows **Created blog post: Publish rules 156**.
Reloading after a successful save does not warn that changes may be lost.
Both posts are on /blog/admin as **Published** with today's date.
Both are at the top of /blog.
In BlogPost both have `isPublished` `true`, `publishedAt` set to the moment of saving, and `description` the text you pasted.
AppEvent has a `Create Requested` and a `Create Success` row for each post, the second with a message like `Create Success | id=<id> | slug=publish-rules`.
steps.note: Today the form keeps every value after a save and the reload still asks whether to leave (see found).

steps.title: Saving a draft
do: Open {page:/blog/create-new-post} (discard any saved work). Type `Draft check` in **Title**, press Tab, leave **Meta description** empty, untick **Publish now** and press **Submit Post**.
Change **Title** to `Draft check 2` and **Slug** to `draft-check-2`, type `Too short.` in **Meta description**, keep **Publish now** unticked and press **Submit Post**.
Open {page:/blog/admin}, {page:/blog} and the BlogPost rows.
expect: The first saves: **Created blog post: Draft check**.
The second is refused with **The meta description must be 120 to 156 characters.**: a description that is filled in must be in range, even on a draft.
**Draft check** is on /blog/admin with the amber **Draft** and **Created** today.
It is not on /blog.
In BlogPost it has `isPublished` `false`, and `publishedAt` and `description` empty.
steps.note: The hint under the box says **Needed to publish.**, yet a half-written description stops a draft too. Empty the box to save a draft.

steps.title: Content blocks: add, fill, reorder and remove
do: On {page:/blog/create-new-post}, press **Add Paragraph**, **Add Heading**, **Add List**, **Add Link** and **Add Paragraph** again.
Type something in each block.
In the list press **Add item** twice, then **Remove** on the second item.
In the link switch between **Internal** and **External**.
Press the down arrow on **Heading 1**, then the up arrow on the last block.
Press **Delete block** on the list and **Delete** on one paragraph.
expect: Each block is a bordered box headed by its type and its number among blocks of that type: **Paragraph 1**, **Heading 1**, **List 1**, **Link 1**, **Paragraph 2**.
Each box has an up and a down arrow, with the tooltips **Move up** and **Move down**.
The top block's up arrow and the bottom block's down arrow are greyed out and do nothing.
The paragraph box has the placeholder **Paragraph text** and a red **Delete**; the heading box has **Heading text**.
The list starts with one box, **List item 1**, beside a **Remove** button; **Add item** adds **List item 2** and **List item 3**, and removing one renumbers the rest.
The link has **Link text (what readers see)**, an address box, and the choice **Internal** (chosen at first) or **External**.
With **Internal** the address placeholder is **Internal path (e.g., /about)** and the hint reads **Will be rendered with internal link to a page of your site.**
With **External** they are **External URL (e.g., https://example.com)** and **Will be rendered with link to a different website.**
Moving swaps a block with its neighbour and keeps what you typed; the numbers follow the new order.
**Delete block** and **Delete** take the block out at once.

steps.title: What the saved post keeps of the blocks
do: On {page:/blog/create-new-post}, type `Block check` in **Title**, press Tab and untick **Publish now**.

Add, in this order: a paragraph `First paragraph with bold tags.`, an empty paragraph, a heading `A heading`, a list with the items `One`, an empty item and `Two`, a list whose only item is empty, and a paragraph `Last paragraph.`
Move the heading to the top and press **Submit Post**.
Open {page:/blog/block-check} and the post's `content` in Prisma Studio.
expect: The post shows the heading **A heading** first.
Then **First paragraph with bold tags.**, with nothing in bold: the server strips anything between `<` and `>`.
Then a list of **One** and **Two**, then **Last paragraph.**
The empty paragraph, the empty list item and the list with nothing in it were not saved.
`content` holds exactly those four blocks, in that order.
steps.note: Anything between angle brackets is removed, so a post cannot quote HTML such as `<title>`. Keep this post for E35.

steps.title: Link blocks: internal, external and refused addresses
do: On {page:/blog/create-new-post}, type `Link check` in **Title**, press Tab and untick **Publish now**.

Add five links: `Contact page`, **Internal**, `/contact`. `Mail us`, **External**, `mailto:hello@bytetoast-studio.com`. `Example`, **External**, `https://example.com`. `No scheme`, **External**, `www.example.com`. `Script`, **External**, `javascript:alert(1)`.
Press **Submit Post** and open {page:/blog/link-check}.
expect: **Contact page** opens /contact in the same tab.
**Mail us** starts a new mail to hello@bytetoast-studio.com.
**Example** opens example.com in a new tab.
Before anything is saved, the form refuses **No scheme** and **Script** with a message that an address must start with `/`, `https://`, `http://`, `mailto:` or `tel:`.
**Script** never becomes a link on the post.
steps.note: Today both are dropped without a word and the form says **Created blog post: Link check** (see found).

steps.title: Tags
do: On {page:/blog/create-new-post}, type `Tag check` in **Title**, press Tab, add the 120-character description and a paragraph, and type `Guides, SEO,  Guides , ,News` in **Tags (comma-separated)**. Press **Submit Post**.
Open {page:/blog/tag-check} and BlogTag in Prisma Studio.
Press **Edit** on **Tag check** in /blog/admin and look at **Tags (comma-separated)**.
Change the tags to `Guides` and press **Update Post**.
After a few seconds, refresh BlogTag.
expect: The post shows three chips, **Guides**, **News** and **SEO**: spaces trimmed, the repeat and the empty entry dropped.
BlogTag gains `Guides` and `SEO`; `News` is the seeded tag, reused rather than added twice.
The edit form's box shows `Guides,News,SEO`.
After the update the post shows only **Guides**.
The `SEO` row is gone from BlogTag, since nothing uses it; `News` stays, because the seeded post still has it.
steps.note: Tags match exactly: `news` would be a tag of its own beside `News`. A post keeps up to 20 tags, each cut to 40 characters. Keep this post for E36.

steps.title: Autosave on the create page
do: On {page:/blog/create-new-post}, type `Autosave check` in **Title** and add a paragraph `Kept?`.
In devtools Application, Local storage, find `createBlogPostDraft:v1`.
Add an image block and choose a picture.
Reload the page and accept the browser's warning.
Press **Click to discard draft**.
expect: Once there is a title, a banner reads **Draft is being autosaved.** with the button **Click to discard draft**.
`createBlogPostDraft:v1` holds the form as JSON and updates a moment after each change.
Reloading first brings up the browser's leave-page warning.
After the reload the title and the paragraph are back.
The image block is back but empty: files are not kept.
**Click to discard draft** empties the form, removes the key and hides the banner.
steps.note: Autosave starts with a title, slug, subtitle, subject, location, author, tags or a block: a description on its own is not saved.

steps.title: Uploading images and choosing the thumbnail
do: On {page:/blog/create-new-post}, type `Image check` in **Title**, press Tab and add the 120-character description.
Press **Add Image**, click the dashed box and choose a JPEG under 5MB.
Press **Add Image** again and drag a PNG under 5MB onto the new box.
Tick **Use as thumbnail** on Image 2, then on Image 1.
Press **Change** on Image 2 and choose another picture.
With devtools Network open, press **Submit Post**.
Look at MediaItem and BlogPostMedia in Prisma Studio, and at the post and its card.
expect: Each new image block shows a dashed box with a cloud icon and **Click or drop an image (max 5MB)**; the file picker offers images only.
A chosen or dropped file replaces the box with a preview; **Change** swaps the preview.
Ticking **Use as thumbnail** on Image 1 unticks it on Image 2: only one thumbnail at a time.
Each image makes a `POST /api/media-services/presign-url`, a `PUT` to the storage host and a `POST /api/media-services/confirm-upload`, and then `POST /api/blog/create-blog-post` answers 201.
**Created blog post: Image check** shows.
MediaItem has two new rows with `resource` `blog`, `kind` `IMAGE` and `bytes` equal to each file's size.
Their keys start `testing/blog/`, then tom's user id, the year and the month.
BlogPostMedia links the post to both images as `GALLERY` (positions 0 and 1), and to Image 1 as `THUMBNAIL` too.
The post shows both images in place, and its card on /blog uses Image 1.
steps.note: Uses four of the 20 upload calls per 15 minutes. Keep this post for E31.

steps.title: Uploading a video
do: On {page:/blog/create-new-post}, type `Video check` in **Title**, press Tab and add the 120-character description.
Press **Add Video** and choose an MP4 under 20MB.
Press **Submit Post** and open {page:/blog/video-check}.
expect: The video block shows **Click or drop a video (max 20MB)**, then a player preview once a file is chosen.
A video block has no **Use as thumbnail** box.
MediaItem has a new row with `kind` `VIDEO`, and BlogPostMedia links it as `EMBED`.
The post shows a player with controls, and it plays.
The card on /blog has no picture.
steps.note: Keep this post for E36.

steps.title: Upload refusals
do: On {page:/blog/create-new-post}, press **Add Image** and choose a picture over 5MB.
Press **Add Video** and choose a video over 20MB.
Drag a video file onto the image box, and a picture onto the video box.
Delete both blocks. Type `Type check` in **Title**, press Tab, add the 120-character description, add an image block and choose a BMP picture.
Press **Submit Post**.
expect: Over 5MB: a browser alert **File too large (>5MB).** and the box stays empty.
Over 20MB: **File too large (>20MB).**
A video dropped on the image box: **Please select an image file.**
A picture dropped on the video box: **Please select a video file.**
The BMP goes into the box, but **Submit Post** shows **Unsupported content type for this resource.** in red at the top of the form.
No post is created and MediaItem has no row for the BMP.
steps.note: The server takes PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF and SVG pictures, and MP4, WebM, QuickTime, Ogg and Matroska video. The server's own size caps are tested in the cross-cutting part. If the bucket's CORS does not allow http://localhost:5173, every upload fails with **Create blog failed.**

steps.title: A refused submit with a file attached
do: On {page:/blog/create-new-post}, type `Retry check` in **Title** and press Tab. Leave **Meta description** empty, keep **Publish now** ticked, and add an image block with a JPEG.
Press **Submit Post**, then look at MediaItem in Prisma Studio.
Put the 120-character description in and press **Submit Post** again.
Look at MediaItem again.
expect: The first press is refused with **Add a meta description (120 to 156 characters) before publishing.**
The second press creates the post.
MediaItem holds one row for the picture: the one the post uses.
steps.note: Today each press uploads the file again. After the second press there are two rows, the first attached to nothing until the daily cleanup deletes it after 24 hours, and every press costs two more of the 20 upload calls allowed per 15 minutes (see found).

steps.title: A duplicate slug when creating
do: On {page:/blog/create-new-post}, type `Welcome to the blog` in **Title**, press Tab, untick **Publish now** and press **Submit Post**.
Change **Title** to `Another post` and **Slug** to `Welcome To The Blog`, and press **Submit Post**.
expect: In red at the top: **Slug must be unique. "welcome-to-the-blog" is already in use**, then a dash and **change the slug and try again.**
With the slug in capitals the server still finds the clash, and the message quotes the slug as you typed it: **"Welcome To The Blog"**.
No second post appears on /blog/admin.
steps.note: The server checks the title and slug, then the description, then whether the slug is taken, so with **Publish now** ticked and no description you get the description message first. The form shows its own wording here instead of the server's.

steps.title: /blog/admin: Show all
do: With the posts made so far (well over five), open {page:/blog/admin}.
Press **Show all**, then **Show less**.
expect: Only the five newest rows show, with a button **Show all** and the total, for example **Show all 14**.
**Show all** lists every post and the button becomes **Show less**, with `aria-expanded` now `true`.
**Show less** goes back to five rows.

steps.title: /blog/edit: the form opens filled in
do: On {page:/blog/admin}, press **Edit** on **Welcome to the blog**.
Change **Title** to something else and look at **Slug**, then put the title back.
expect: The address is `/blog/edit/<id>`, and the header reads **Edit Blog Post** and **ID:** with the post's id.
The tab reads **Edit Blog Post | Byte Toast Studio** and the `robots` meta is `noindex,nofollow`.
The form, headed **Edit Blog Post**, has **Title** `Welcome to the blog`, **Slug** `welcome-to-the-blog` and **Subtitle** `First post (ByteToast Studio seed).`
The description is filled in and the counter reads **135 of 120 to 156 characters. Needed to publish.**
**Subject** is `News`, **Location** is empty, **Author Name** is `Admin` and **Tags** is `Announcement,News`.
**Published (untick to hide as a draft)** is ticked.
**Content Sections** holds **Paragraph 1**, **Heading 1**, **List 1** with three items, and **Link 1** set to **Internal** with `/contact`.
There is no autosave banner, and the button reads **Update Post**.
Changing **Title** here does not change **Slug**.

steps.title: Editing and saving
do: On the edit page for **Welcome to the blog** (opened with **Edit** on /blog/admin), change **Subtitle** to `Edited subtitle`.
Press **Update Post**.
Open {page:/blog/welcome-to-the-blog}, and look at the row in BlogPost and at AppEvent.
expect: As soon as you type, a banner reads **Draft changes are being autosaved.** with **Discard draft**.
The button reads **Updating**, with an ellipsis, while it saves.
**Updated: Welcome to the blog** shows in green at the top of the form.
The banner goes and the form still shows your change.
The post shows **Edited subtitle**.
In BlogPost `updatedAt` has moved on, while `publishedAt` and `isPublished` are unchanged.
AppEvent has an `Update Requested` and an `Update Success` row.
steps.note: Today, when the edit page was opened from /blog/admin or by its address, the form blinks into a grey loading box and comes back without the green message (see found). The change is saved all the same.

steps.title: Edit refusals
do: On the edit page for **Welcome to the blog**, clear **Title** and press **Update Post**.
Put the title back, change **Meta description** to `Too short.` and press **Update Post**.
Clear **Meta description** and press **Update Post**.
Press **Discard draft**.
expect: With no title: **Please provide both a title and a slug.**, and nothing is sent.
With `Too short.`: **The meta description must be 120 to 156 characters.**
With the description empty on a published post: **Add a meta description (120 to 156 characters) before publishing.**
Each message is bold red in a box at the top of the form, and the post itself does not change.
**Discard draft** puts the saved values back in the form.

steps.title: Changing the slug
do: On the edit page for **Welcome to the blog**, change **Slug** to `draft-post` and press **Update Post**.
Change **Slug** to `Welcome Renamed!` and press **Update Post**.
Open {page:/blog/welcome-renamed} and {page:/blog/welcome-to-the-blog}.
Change the slug back to `welcome-to-the-blog` and save.
expect: With `draft-post`: in red, **Slug must be unique**, then a dash and **another post already uses it.**
`Welcome Renamed!` saves, and **Slug** then shows `welcome-renamed`.
/blog/welcome-renamed opens the post.
/blog/welcome-to-the-blog shows **Post not found** while the slug is changed.
Changing it back makes the old address work again.
steps.note: Nothing sends the old address on to the new one.

steps.title: Unpublishing clears publishedAt
do: On the edit page for **Welcome to the blog**, untick **Published (untick to hide as a draft)** and press **Update Post**.
Look at {page:/blog/admin}, {page:/blog} and the BlogPost row.
In a private window, open {page:/blog/welcome-to-the-blog}.
expect: The row on /blog/admin turns to the amber **Draft**, with **Created** and its creation date.
In BlogPost, `isPublished` is `false` and `publishedAt` is empty.
/blog no longer lists it.
Signed out, the post shows **Post not found**.

steps.title: Republishing gives a new date
do: Note the post's `createdAt` in BlogPost.
On its edit page, tick **Published** again and press **Update Post**.
Look at the BlogPost row, {page:/blog/admin}, {page:/blog} and the post's `article:published_time`.
expect: `publishedAt` is set again, to the moment you saved: clearly later than `createdAt`, where the seed had set both at the same moment.
/blog/admin shows **Published** with today's date.
On /blog the post moves to the top (newest publish date first), dated today.
`article:published_time` on the post is the new time.

steps.title: Publishing the seeded draft
do: On {page:/blog/admin}, press **Edit** on **Draft post**.
Tick **Published** and press **Update Post**.
Put the 120-character description in **Meta description** and press **Update Post**.
Log out and open {page:/blog/draft-post} and {page:/blog}.
expect: The counter starts at **0 of 120 to 156 characters. Needed to publish.**
The first press is refused: **Add a meta description (120 to 156 characters) before publishing.**
With the description it saves, and /blog/admin shows **Draft post** as **Published** today.
Signed out, /blog/draft-post opens.
/blog lists **Draft post** first.

steps.title: Media taken out of a post is deleted
do: Open the edit page for **Image check** (from E18) and note both image keys in MediaItem.
Press **Delete** on Image 2 and press **Update Post**.
After a few seconds, look at MediaItem, BlogPostMedia and the bucket in your storage provider's dashboard.
Press **Change** on the remaining image, choose a different picture, leave **Use as thumbnail** ticked and press **Update Post**.
Untick **Use as thumbnail** and press **Update Post**.
expect: The form opens with both images previewed and **Use as thumbnail** ticked on Image 1.
Nothing is deleted until **Update Post** is pressed.
After saving without Image 2, its MediaItem row and its file in the bucket are gone, and BlogPostMedia keeps only Image 1's rows.
After **Change**, the new picture has its own MediaItem row, the old picture's row and file are deleted, and the card on /blog shows the new picture.
After unticking, the card on /blog has no picture and the `THUMBNAIL` row is gone, but the picture stays in the post and in MediaItem.
steps.note: The deleting runs after the response, so give it a moment. A browser or CDN can keep showing a cached copy of a deleted file's address.

steps.title: Autosave on the edit page
do: On the edit page for **Welcome to the blog**, change **Subject** to `Autosaved`.
In devtools Local storage, find `editBlogPostDraft:v2:<id>`.
Reload and accept the browser's warning.
Look at **Subject**, the banner and Local storage.
Reload once more.
Press **Discard draft** if it is there, or put **Subject** back to `News` and save.
expect: **Draft changes are being autosaved.** with **Discard draft** shows as soon as you type.
`editBlogPostDraft:v2:<id>` holds the form.
Reloading first brings up the browser's leave-page warning.
After the reload **Subject** reads `Autosaved` and the banner is still there, so you can tell the change is not saved.
The key stays in Local storage, so the second reload still keeps the change.
**Discard draft** brings back the saved values and removes the key.
steps.note: Today the restored change shows with no banner and no **Discard draft**, and the key is deleted a moment after the page loads, so the second reload silently loses it (see found).

steps.title: An edit address for a post that does not exist
do: Open {page:/blog/edit/not-a-real-id}.
expect: The header reads **Edit Blog Post** and **ID: not-a-real-id**.
Instead of the form, a box reads **Failed to find blog post(s).**

steps.title: Editing from a post's EDIT link, then reloading
do: Open {page:/blog/welcome-to-the-blog} and press **EDIT**.
Change **Subtitle** to `Changed via EDIT` and press **Update Post**.
Reload the edit page and look at **Subtitle**.
expect: **Updated: Welcome to the blog** shows in green.
After the reload **Subtitle** reads `Changed via EDIT`, the saved value.
steps.note: Today the reload brings back the subtitle from before your change, because the page reuses the copy the post page put in the browser's history; pressing **Update Post** then would write that old version back (see found). Open the edit page from /blog/admin to get the saved values.

steps.title: Deleting a post
do: On {page:/blog/admin}, press **Delete** on **Block check**.
Open {page:/blog/block-check}.
expect: A dialog asks you to confirm, with a way to cancel, before anything is deleted.
After confirming, the button shows a spinner and **Deleting**, then a green box above the list reads **Deleted "Block check".**
The row disappears and the other rows stay.
/blog/block-check shows **Post not found**, for an admin too.
steps.note: Today **Delete** deletes straight away, with no question (see found). Every other delete in the admin area asks first.

steps.title: What a delete removes
do: Note the MediaItem key of **Video check** (E19), and that **Tag check** (E16) is the only post tagged `Guides`.
Delete both posts from {page:/blog/admin}.
After a few seconds, look at BlogPost, BlogPostMedia, MediaItem and BlogTag, and at the bucket.
Open {page:/blog}.
expect: Both BlogPost rows and their BlogPostMedia rows are gone.
The video's MediaItem row and its file in the bucket are deleted.
`Guides` is gone from BlogTag; `Announcement` and `News` stay while the seeded post has them.
/blog shows neither post.

steps.title: Rebuild hook: not set
do: Make sure `FRONTEND_BUILD_HOOK_URL` is empty in the server env (as in `server/.env.example`) and restart the server.
Watching the server terminal, create a published post `Hook check` with the 120-character description.
Change its subtitle on its edit page and save.
Delete it from /blog/admin.
expect: The terminal shows `POST /api/blog/create-blog-post 201`, `PATCH /api/blog/update-blog-post/<id> 200` and `DELETE /api/blog/delete-blog-post/<id> 200`.
No line starts `[rebuild]` and no other request appears: without a hook nothing is called and nothing is logged.
All three actions succeed as normal.

steps.title: Rebuild hook: set
do: Set `FRONTEND_BUILD_HOOK_URL=http://localhost:4000/rebuild-hook-test` in the server env and restart the server.
Watching the terminal, create a published post `Hook check`.
Change its subtitle and save.
Delete it.
expect: With the create's `201` line come `POST /rebuild-hook-test 404` and `[rebuild] build hook returned 404 (blog post created)`.
The edit brings the same pair, ending `(blog post updated)`.
The delete brings the same pair, ending `(blog post deleted)`.
Each action still succeeds with its usual message in the browser: the hook is called after the response.
steps.note: This address points the hook at the server itself, which has no such route, so you can watch it being called. A real Netlify, Vercel or Cloudflare build hook answers 200, logs nothing here and starts a build of the site.

steps.title: Rebuild hook: only changes a visitor could see
do: With the hook still set as in E38, create `Hook draft` with **Publish now** unticked.
Change its subtitle and save.
Tick **Published**, add the 120-character description and save.
Untick **Published** and save.
Change its subtitle again and save.
Delete it.
expect: Creating the draft calls nothing: no `POST /rebuild-hook-test` line.
Editing it while it is still a draft calls nothing.
Publishing it calls the hook, ending `(blog post updated)`.
Unpublishing calls the hook too, because visitors could see the post before.
Editing it as a draft again calls nothing.
Deleting it as a draft calls nothing.

steps.title: Rebuild hook: a hook that fails
do: Set `FRONTEND_BUILD_HOOK_URL=http://localhost:9/` (nothing listens there) and restart the server.
Create a published post `Hook fail check`.
expect: The browser shows **Created blog post: Hook fail check** as normal.
The terminal shows `[rebuild] build hook failed (blog post created): fetch failed`.
The server keeps running.
steps.note: Empty `FRONTEND_BUILD_HOOK_URL` again and restart the server when done, then reseed.

parts.part: Admin: users, roles and the audit log
parts.intro: The Admin menu in the navbar for each role, what the admin guards do for each role, /admin/users (the list, search, filters, role changes, deactivating, reactivating, deleting, and every rule the server enforces) and the audit log at /admin/events. Accounts: `user@gmail.com`, `tom@gmail.com` (ADMIN) and `dev@gmail.com` (DEVELOPER), plus two throwaway accounts you register in R6, Account R1 and Account R2, on addresses you can read. Only the throwaways are promoted, deactivated or deleted, so the seeded accounts end as they began. By the end both throwaways are deleted and the audit log has been emptied (R39), so run this part after any other part that wants to read the log. Reseed with `npx prisma db seed` in `server/` to start again (it wipes every table). Run the tests in order: each builds on the one before. You need three sessions open at once: the main window, a private window, and a second browser (or a second browser profile), because private windows share one set of cookies between them. Keep `npx prisma studio` (in `server/`) open to check the database. Many rules can only be tried from the browser console, because the page hides the buttons that would break them. For those, open devtools on any page of the site, in the window signed in as the account named, and paste this helper (Chrome asks you to type `allow pasting` the first time): `const api = (method, path, body) => fetch('http://localhost:4000' + path, { method, credentials: 'include', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: body ? JSON.stringify(body) : undefined }).then(async (r) => { const j = await r.json(); console.log(r.status, j); return j; }); const idOf = async (name) => (await api('GET', '/api/users/admin/get-all-users?search=' + encodeURIComponent(name))).data.users.find((u) => u.name === name).id;` It prints each answer's status code and body. Paste it again after every reload. Change `http://localhost:4000` if your `VITE_API_URL` points somewhere else. `idOf('Account R1')` looks an account's id up by its name, and only works for an ADMIN or a DEVELOPER.

steps.title: Navbar as a USER: no Admin menu
do: In the main window, sign in as user@gmail.com on {page:/login}, with the window at least 1024px wide.
Read along the navbar.
Narrow the window below 1024px, press the menu button at the top right and read down the list.
expect: The bar holds **Home**, **About**, **Reviews**, **Gallery**, **Contact**, **FAQ**, **Links**, **Blog**, **Guest Book**, **Booking**, **Newsletter**, a **Legal** dropdown, **Account** and **Logout**.
There is no **Admin** item.
**Login** and **Sign Up** have gone now you are signed in.
The phone menu lists the same items, with **Legal** as its only toggle and no **Admin**.

steps.title: Navbar as an ADMIN: the Admin dropdown without Audit Log
do: Press **Logout**, then sign in as tom@gmail.com with the window at least 1024px wide.
Click **Admin** in the navbar.
With the panel open and the focus still on **Admin**, press **Escape**.
Open it again and click somewhere on the page outside the navbar.
Open it again and click each link in turn, coming back and opening it each time.
Narrow the window below 1024px, open the menu and press **Admin**.
expect: An **Admin** button with a small caret sits after **Legal** and before **Account**.
It opens a panel under it listing **Dashboard**, **Contact Forms**, **Callback Requests**, **Bookings**, **Newsletter**, **Blog Admin**, **New Blog Post** and **Users**, in that order.
There is no **Audit Log** link.
**Escape** closes the panel, and so does a click outside the navbar.

The eight links open `/admin`, `/admin/contact-forms`, `/admin/callback-forms`, `/admin/booking-admin`, `/admin/newsletter-overview`, `/blog/admin`, `/blog/create-new-post` and `/admin/users`, and each page stays open rather than sending you home.
In the phone menu **Admin** opens the same eight links beneath it, and its caret flips upside down.
steps.note: The dropdown opens on a click only, never on hover. The **Manage** links on the /admin dashboard are covered in the admin-inbox part.

steps.title: Navbar as a DEVELOPER: Audit Log added
do: Press **Logout**, then sign in as dev@gmail.com at desktop width.
Click **Admin**.
Click **Audit Log**.
Narrow the window below 1024px, open the menu and press **Admin**.
expect: The panel lists the same eight links as for tom, then a ninth, **Audit Log**, at the bottom.
**Audit Log** opens `/admin/events`, headed **Audit Log**.
The phone menu's **Admin** toggle shows the same nine links.

steps.title: A USER opening the admin pages
do: Press **Logout** and sign in as user@gmail.com.

Open each of these in turn by typing it in the address bar: {page:/admin}, {page:/admin/contact-forms}, {page:/admin/callback-forms}, {page:/admin/booking-admin}, {page:/admin/newsletter-overview}, {page:/admin/users}, {page:/admin/events}, {page:/blog/admin}, {page:/blog/create-new-post} and `/blog/edit/any-id`.
After the last one, press the browser's Back button.
Open the console, paste the helper from the intro and run `await api('GET', '/api/users/admin/get-all-users')`.
Run `await api('GET', '/api/events/get-paginated-events')`.
expect: Every one of them ends on the home page at `/`, after a brief spinner at most.
No admin heading, list or data shows before the redirect.
Nothing on the home page says why you were sent there.
Back never brings an admin address back: each one was replaced by `/` in the history.
You are still signed in: **Account** and **Logout** are still in the navbar.
The first console call prints `403` with **This action requires an admin or developer role.**
The second prints `403` with **This action requires a developer role.**
steps.note: Signed out, the same addresses go to /login and return after signing in: the accounts part covers that. Both console refusals are written to the audit log (R32).

steps.title: An ADMIN opening the audit log
do: Press **Logout**, sign in as tom@gmail.com and open {page:/admin/events} from the address bar.
Open the console, paste the helper and run `await api('GET', '/api/events/get-paginated-events')`.
Run `await api('DELETE', '/api/events/delete-all-events')`.
expect: /admin/events lands on the home page at `/`.
You stay signed in, and the **Admin** dropdown is still there, without **Audit Log**.
Both console calls print `403` with **This action requires a developer role.**
Nothing is deleted: the audit log still holds its events when dev opens it in R26.

steps.title: Register the two throwaway accounts
do: In the private window open {page:/sign-up}.

Type `Account R1` in **Username**, an address you can read in **Email** (for example `you+r1@yourdomain.com`), `TestPass1!` in **Password** and **Confirm Password**, tick the terms box and press **Register Now**.
Press **Logout**.
Register again with **Username** `Account R2`, a second address you can read (for example `you+r2@yourdomain.com`) and the same password, then press **Logout**.
Run `npx prisma studio` in `server/` and open the `User` model.
expect: Each registration lands on /account, signed in.
Each address receives **Byte Toast Studio: Verify email address**.
The `User` model has both rows, `name` `Account R1` and `Account R2`, with `role` `USER`, `isActive` `true` and `emailVerified` `false`.
steps.note: Never use a seeded address here: they are strangers' real inboxes. Leave the verification links unclicked so R8 can see the unverified badge. Sign-up itself is tested in the accounts part.

steps.title: /admin/users: the page
do: In the main window, still signed in as tom@gmail.com, open {page:/admin/users}.
In devtools, find the robots meta tag in the head.
expect: The tab reads **User Admin | Byte Toast Studio**.
The page heading is **User Admin**, followed by a blue bar headed **Users**.

A filter box holds **Search name or email** (a search field), **Role** (**All roles**, **User**, **Admin**, **Developer**) and **Status** (**All statuses**, **Active**, **Deactivated**), set to **All roles** and **All statuses** to begin with.
Below it, one card per account, newest first and two to a row on a wide screen: **Account R2**, **Account R1**, **Dev**, **Admin**, **User**.
Under the cards: **Previous**, **Page 1 of 1 (5 total)** and **Next**, with both buttons greyed out.
The robots tag reads `noindex,nofollow`.
steps.note: Accounts registered by other parts show here too, which changes the order and the totals in this part. The list holds 20 accounts a page.

steps.title: What a user card shows
do: On {page:/admin/users}, read the **Account R1** card.
Read the **User** card.
Hover over the round red cross at the top right of the Account R1 card.
On the Account R1 card choose **Admin** in **Role**, then choose **User** again. Do not save.
expect: Heading **Account R1**, then **Email:** with its address and **Joined:** with today's date.
Three small badges: `USER`, a green **Active** and a yellow **Email not verified**.
The **User** card's third badge is a green **Email verified**.
A **Role** drop-down showing **User**, a greyed-out **Save role** button and a yellow **Deactivate** button.
The cross shows the tooltip **Delete Account R1**.
Choosing **Admin** makes **Save role** clickable, and going back to **User** greys it out again.

steps.title: Cards an ADMIN cannot change
do: On {page:/admin/users}, look at the **Admin** card, which is yours.
Look at the **Dev** card.
Open the **Role** list on the Account R1 card.
In devtools, inspect the **Role** drop-down on the **Dev** card.
expect: On your own card the drop-down, **Save role**, **Deactivate** and the cross are all greyed out and do nothing when clicked.
Under them, in small grey text: **This is your account**, a dash, then **manage it from your account page.**
The **Dev** card is greyed out the same way, its drop-down shows **Developer**, and its note reads **Only a developer can manage developer accounts.**
The Account R1 list offers **User** and **Admin** only. There is no **Developer**.
The **User** card is not locked.
The locked drop-down has an `aria-describedby` naming the note's id (`user-note-<id>`), so a screen reader reads out why it is locked.
steps.note: The page only mirrors the server's rules. R14 to R19 try each rule against the server directly.

steps.title: Search and filters
do: On {page:/admin/users}, type `account r` in **Search name or email** and wait a moment.
Replace it with `TOM@GMAIL`.
Clear the search. Set **Role** to **Admin**, then **Developer**, then **User**.
Set **Role** back to **All roles** and **Status** to **Deactivated**.
Set **Status** to **Active**.
Type `nobody-here` in the search, then clear it and set **Status** to **All statuses**.
expect: The list updates by itself just after you stop typing. There is no search button, and Enter does nothing.
`account r` leaves the **Account R2** and **Account R1** cards: the search matches names.
`TOM@GMAIL` leaves only the **Admin** card: it matches addresses and ignores case.
**Admin** leaves only the **Admin** card, **Developer** only **Dev**, and **User** leaves **Account R2**, **Account R1** and **User**.
**Deactivated** shows **No users match these filters.** and the pager disappears.
**Active** shows all five cards.
`nobody-here` shows **No users match these filters.**

steps.title: One account's details from the API
do: On {page:/admin/users}, open the console and paste the helper.
Run `await api('GET', '/api/users/admin/get-user-by-id/' + await idOf('Account R1'))`.
Run `await api('GET', '/api/users/admin/get-user-by-id/no-such-id')`.
expect: `idOf` first prints `200` and the list it searched, with `users`, `total`, `page` `1` and `pageSize` `20`.
The lookup prints `200` and a `user` with `id`, `name` `Account R1`, `email`, `emailVerified` `false`, `role` `USER`, `isActive` `true`, `image` `null`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`.
Nothing about passwords, sessions or sign-in accounts is in it.
The unknown id prints `404` with **Failed to find user(s).**
steps.note: The page has no separate details view: the card shows everything an admin needs. Unlike the list, this lookup is written to the audit log as **Get By Id Success** (R31).

steps.title: Change a role: Account R1 to Admin
do: In the second browser, sign in as Account R1 (`TestPass1!`) and stay on /account. Its navbar has no **Admin**.
In the main window, on {page:/admin/users}, use the keyboard: Tab to the Account R1 card's **Role**, choose **Admin** with the arrow keys, Tab to **Save role** and press Enter.
Press Tab once more and see where the focus goes.
Reload the main window and look at the card, then at Account R1 in Prisma Studio.
In the second browser, look at the navbar, then reload it and open **Users** from the **Admin** dropdown.
expect: Green text above the list: **Account R1 is now Admin.**
The card's badge reads `ADMIN`, its drop-down shows **Admin** and **Save role** is greyed out again.
The next Tab moves on within the card (to **Deactivate**), not to **Skip to main content** at the top of the page.
After the reload the card still reads `ADMIN`, and Prisma Studio shows `role` `ADMIN`.
Account R1's navbar only changes once it reloads. Then it has the **Admin** dropdown with the same eight links as tom's, and no **Audit Log**.
Account R1 can open /admin/users. Its own card carries the self note, **Dev** is locked with the developer note, and tom's **Admin** card is not locked.
steps.note: An ADMIN may change, deactivate or delete another ADMIN, so press nothing on tom's card from Account R1. The new role counts from Account R1's next request, because the server reads the role from the database every time, not from the session.

steps.title: The role is checked on every request
do: Leave Account R1 on /admin/users in the second browser.
In the main window, set Account R1's **Role** to **User** and press **Save role**.
In the second browser, without reloading, change the filter box's **Role** to **Admin**.
Reload the second browser.
expect: The main window says **Account R1 is now User.** and the badge reads `USER`.
In the second browser the list is replaced by red text: **This action requires an admin or developer role.**
After the reload, Account R1 is sent to the home page and the **Admin** dropdown has gone.
Account R1 is still signed in, with **Account** and **Logout** in the navbar.

steps.title: Rule: an ADMIN cannot grant Developer
do: On {page:/admin/users}, paste the helper in the console.
Run `await api('PATCH', '/api/users/admin/change-user-role', { userId: await idOf('Account R2'), newRole: 'DEVELOPER' })`.
Reload the page.
expect: The call prints `403` with **Only a developer can grant or remove the developer role.**
Account R2 is still `USER`.
steps.note: The page never offers **Developer** to an ADMIN (R9), so the console is the only way to ask.

steps.title: Rule: an invalid role, a missing role, an unknown account
do: In the console on {page:/admin/users}, with the helper pasted, run `const r2 = await idOf('Account R2');`.
Run `await api('PATCH', '/api/users/admin/change-user-role', { userId: r2, newRole: 'OWNER' })`.
Run `await api('PATCH', '/api/users/admin/change-user-role', { userId: r2 })`.
Run `await api('PATCH', '/api/users/admin/deactivate-user/no-such-id')`.
Run `await api('GET', '/api/users/admin/get-all-users?role=OWNER')`.
Run `const me = (await api('GET', '/api/users/user/get-logged-in-user')).data.user.id;`, then `await api('PATCH', '/api/users/admin/change-user-role', { userId: me, newRole: 'OWNER' })`.
Reload the page.
expect: `OWNER` prints `400` with **Role must be USER, ADMIN or DEVELOPER.**
Leaving out `newRole` prints `400` with **Missing fields in request**
The unknown id prints `404` with **Failed to find user(s).**
The list with `role=OWNER` prints `400` with **Role must be USER, ADMIN or DEVELOPER.**
`OWNER` on your own account gets the role message too, not the self one: the role is checked before who the target is.
Account R2 and your own card are unchanged.

steps.title: Rule: an ADMIN cannot act on their own account
do: On {page:/admin/users}, paste the helper again and run `const me = (await api('GET', '/api/users/user/get-logged-in-user')).data.user.id;`.
Run `await api('PATCH', '/api/users/admin/change-user-role', { userId: me, newRole: 'USER' })`.
Run `await api('PATCH', '/api/users/admin/deactivate-user/' + me)`.
Run `await api('PATCH', '/api/users/admin/reactivate-user/' + me)`.
Run `await api('DELETE', '/api/users/admin/delete-user-by-id/' + me)`.
Reload the page.
expect: The first call prints `200` with your own `user`, `role` `ADMIN`.
Each of the four actions prints `403` with **You can't change your own role or status, or delete yourself, from the admin panel.**
Your card still reads `ADMIN` and **Active**, and you are still signed in.
steps.note: Your own account is managed from /account, which the account-page part covers. Deleting it there needs your password.

steps.title: /admin/users as a DEVELOPER, and granting Developer
do: In the main window, as tom, open {page:/admin/users} and leave it untouched (no reload) until R18.
In the private window, sign in as dev@gmail.com and open {page:/admin/users}.
Open the **Role** list on several cards.
On the Account R1 card choose **Developer** and press **Save role**.
expect: Every **Role** list offers **User**, **Admin** and **Developer**.
The **Dev** card, yours, is locked with the self note.
Tom's **Admin** card is not locked.
Green **Account R1 is now Developer.**, and the badge reads `DEVELOPER`.
steps.note: A DEVELOPER may change, deactivate or delete another DEVELOPER or an ADMIN, so press nothing on tom's card.

steps.title: Rule: an ADMIN cannot act on a DEVELOPER
do: In tom's window, which has not been reloaded, the Account R1 card still shows `USER`. Press its **Deactivate**, then **Confirm**.
Reload the page.
Paste the helper and run `const r1 = await idOf('Account R1');`.
Run `await api('PATCH', '/api/users/admin/change-user-role', { userId: r1, newRole: 'USER' })`.
Run `await api('PATCH', '/api/users/admin/deactivate-user/' + r1)`, then the same with `reactivate-user` in place of `deactivate-user`.
Run `await api('DELETE', '/api/users/admin/delete-user-by-id/' + r1)`.
In the private window, as dev, reload {page:/admin/users}.
expect: After **Confirm**, red text above the list: **Only a developer can manage developer accounts.** The card still shows **Active**.
After the reload the card reads `DEVELOPER`, its controls are greyed out and its note reads **Only a developer can manage developer accounts.**
Each of the four console calls prints `403` with **Only a developer can manage developer accounts.**
Taking Developer away (`newRole: 'USER'`) gets this message, not **Only a developer can grant or remove the developer role.**: the developer check comes first.
Dev's list still shows Account R1 as `DEVELOPER` and **Active**.

steps.title: A DEVELOPER removes Developer, and cannot act on themselves
do: In the private window, on the Account R1 card choose **User** and press **Save role**.
Paste the helper and run `const me = (await api('GET', '/api/users/user/get-logged-in-user')).data.user.id;`.
Run `await api('PATCH', '/api/users/admin/change-user-role', { userId: me, newRole: 'ADMIN' })`.
Run `await api('PATCH', '/api/users/admin/deactivate-user/' + me)`.
Run `await api('DELETE', '/api/users/admin/delete-user-by-id/' + me)`.
Reload the page.
expect: Green **Account R1 is now User.**, and the badge reads `USER`.
Each of the three actions prints `403` with **You can't change your own role or status, or delete yourself, from the admin panel.**
The **Dev** card still reads `DEVELOPER` and **Active**.

steps.title: Deactivate: the confirm dialog
do: In the second browser, press **Logout**, sign in as Account R2 and stay on /account.
In the main window, reload {page:/admin/users}, Tab to **Deactivate** on the Account R2 card and press Enter.
Press **Cancel**.
Press Enter on **Deactivate** again, then press **Escape**.
Press Enter on **Deactivate** again, Tab to **Confirm** and press Enter.
Press Tab once.
In Prisma Studio, look at Account R2 in the `User` model, then at the `Session` model.
expect: A dialog opens over a darkened page, headed **Deactivate User**, saying **Deactivate Account R2? They will be signed out everywhere and can't sign in until reactivated.**
Two buttons: a red **Cancel**, which has the focus, and a green **Confirm**. Tab moves between them and never leaves the dialog.
The page behind does not scroll while the dialog is open.
**Cancel** and **Escape** each close it with nothing changed, and the focus is back on **Deactivate**.
After **Confirm**: green **Account R2 has been deactivated.**, a red **Deactivated** badge, and the yellow button has become a green **Reactivate**.
The Tab after **Confirm** moves on within the Account R2 card, not to **Skip to main content** at the top of the page.
Account R2's `isActive` is `false`, and the `Session` model holds no row with its `userId`.

steps.title: The deactivated account's open session
do: In the second browser, still on /account, look at the navbar without reloading.
Reload the page.
On /login, sign in as Account R2 with `TestPass1!`.
expect: Before the reload nothing has changed on screen: **Account** and **Logout** are still there, because the browser has not been told.
The reload ends on /login, and the navbar shows **Login** and **Sign Up** instead.
Signing in fails with **This account has been deactivated. Please contact support.** in red under **Sign in**, and you stay on /login.
Prisma Studio still shows no `Session` row for Account R2.
steps.note: The reload's failed session check is written to the audit log as **no-validation** (R32); the refused sign-in is not logged. The accounts part covers the sign-in refusal from the login side.

steps.title: Finding deactivated accounts
do: On {page:/admin/users}, set **Status** to **Deactivated**.
Set it to **Active**.
Set it back to **All statuses**.
expect: **Deactivated** shows only the Account R2 card, with its red **Deactivated** badge and green **Reactivate** button, and **Page 1 of 1 (1 total)**.
**Active** shows every card except Account R2.
**All statuses** shows all five again.

steps.title: Reactivate
do: On the Account R2 card, press **Reactivate**.
Look at Account R2 in Prisma Studio.
Look at the second browser, then sign in there as Account R2 again from the same /login page.
expect: No dialog opens: the change is immediate.
Green **Account R2 has been reactivated.**, a green **Active** badge, and the yellow **Deactivate** button is back.
`isActive` is `true` again.
Before signing in, the second browser still shows **Login** and **Sign Up**: reactivating gives back no session.
Account R2 signs in and lands on /account, the page it was sent away from.

steps.title: Delete an account, with its confirm dialog
do: Keep Account R2 signed in in the second browser.
In the main window, press the round red cross on the Account R2 card, then **Cancel**.
Tab to the cross again, press Enter, Tab to **Confirm** and press Enter.
Press Tab once.
In Prisma Studio, look at the `User`, `Session`, `Account` and `AppEvent` models.
Reload the second browser.
expect: The dialog is headed **Delete User** and says **Permanently delete Account R2 and their avatar? This cannot be undone.**
**Cancel** leaves the card where it was.
After **Confirm**: green **Account R2 has been deleted.**, the list reloads without Account R2, and the pager reads **Page 1 of 1 (4 total)**.
The Tab after **Confirm** stays in the list rather than jumping to **Skip to main content**.
There is no `User` row for Account R2, and no `Session` or `Account` row with its id.
Its `AppEvent` rows are still there, with `actorId` and `targetId` now empty.
The second browser's reload ends on /login, signed out, with **Login** and **Sign Up** in the navbar.
steps.note: To check the avatar clean-up too, give Account R2 an avatar on /account first (the account-page part covers uploading one): its `MediaItem` row and its file are deleted with the account. The address can be registered again afterwards.

steps.title: A role typed in lower case in the database
do: In Prisma Studio, set Account R1's `role` to `admin`, in lower case, and save.
In the second browser, sign in as Account R1.
Look at the navbar, then open {page:/admin/users}.
In the console, paste the helper and run `await api('GET', '/api/users/admin/get-all-users')`.
In the main window, as tom, reload {page:/admin/users} and look at the Account R1 card.
In Prisma Studio, set the `role` back to `USER` and save.
expect: Account R1 gets the **Admin** dropdown, as an `ADMIN` does.
/admin/users opens for Account R1.
The console prints `200` with the list: the server reads `admin` as `ADMIN`.
Tom's view shows the badge `ADMIN` on the Account R1 card.
steps.note: In practice the first two fail: the browser compares roles letter for letter, so the dropdown is missing and /admin/users sends Account R1 home (see found). It matters because the first ADMIN of a new site is made by editing this column by hand.

steps.title: /admin/events: the page
do: In the main window, press **Logout** and sign in as dev@gmail.com. Close the private window.
Open {page:/admin/events}.
In devtools, find the robots meta tag in the head.
expect: The tab reads **Audit Log | Byte Toast Studio**.
The page heading is **Audit Log**, then a blue bar headed **Events** with a red **Delete All** button at its right.

A filter box: **Search message or action**, **Level** (**All levels**, **Debug**, **Info**, **Warning**, **Error**, **Critical**), **Domain** (**All domains**, **Users**, **Contact**, **Guest book**, **Reviews**, **Newsletter**, **Events**, **Blog**, **Booking**, **Auth**, **System**) and **Status** (**All statuses**, **Open**, **Acknowledged**, **Resolved**, **Ignored**).
One card per event, newest at the top, at most 25 on a page.
Under them **Previous**, **Page 1 of N (T total)** and **Next**, with **Previous** greyed out.
The robots tag reads `noindex,nofollow`.

steps.title: What an event card shows
do: On {page:/admin/events}, read the top card.
Type `Change Role` in the search, read a card, then clear the search.
Hover over the round red cross at the top right of a card.
expect: A row of small badges: the level (`INFO` in blue, `WARNING` in yellow), the status (`OPEN` in yellow), the domain (such as `users`), the status code (such as `200`), then the date and time.
The action as the card's heading, such as **Change Role Success**, with the message under it cut to two lines.
A **Status** drop-down showing **Open**, and a **Show details** button at the right.
A **Change Role Success** message starts `Change Role Success | targetId=`.
The cross shows the tooltip **Delete event**.

steps.title: An event's details: a role change
do: Type `Change Role` in **Search**.
On the bottom card, tom's change in R12, press **Show details**.
Press **Hide details**.
expect: Four **Change Role Success** cards, newest first: dev's from R19 and R17, then tom's from R13 and R12.
The message is no longer cut short, and the button reads **Hide details**.
**Message**: `Change Role Success | targetId=<Account R1's id> | targetEmail=<its address> | targetRole=ADMIN | isActive=true`.
**Action**: **Change Role Success**. **Status code**: `200`.
**Request**: `PATCH /api/users/admin/change-user-role`.
**Request ID**: a UUID, such as `1b9d6bcd-bbfd-4b2d-9b5d-ab8dfbbd4bed`.
**Actor**: `Admin <tom@gmail.com>`. **Target**: `Account R1 <its address>`.
**Event ID**, then **Metadata** showing `previousRole` `USER` and `newRole` `ADMIN`.
There is no **Stack** row.
**Hide details** folds it away again.

steps.title: The Request ID matches the response header
do: Open devtools on the Network tab, then paste the helper in the console.
Run `await api('PATCH', '/api/users/admin/deactivate-user/no-such-id')`.
In the Network tab click that request and read its response headers.
Reload {page:/admin/events} and press **Show details** on the top card.
expect: The console prints `404` with **Failed to find user(s).**
The response carries an `x-request-id` header holding a UUID.
The top card is a **not-found** event: level `WARNING`, domain `users`, status code `404`, message **Failed to find user(s).**
Its **Request ID** is the same UUID as the header.
**Request**: `PATCH /api/users/admin/deactivate-user/no-such-id`. **Actor**: `Dev <dev@gmail.com>`. **Target**: a dash.
steps.note: Page code cannot read this header, because CORS does not expose it. Only devtools shows it.

steps.title: Refusals in the log
do: Set **Domain** to **Users** and **Level** to **Warning**.
Press **Show details** on a **no-permission** card and on a **bad-request** card.
expect: Every refusal from R14 to R19 has a card, with the action **no-permission** (`403`) or **bad-request** (`400`) and level `WARNING`.

Their messages are the ones the console printed: **Only a developer can grant or remove the developer role.**, **Role must be USER, ADMIN or DEVELOPER.**, **Missing fields in request**, **You can't change your own role or status, or delete yourself, from the admin panel.** and **Only a developer can manage developer accounts.**
The unknown ids from R11, R15 and R29 show as **not-found** (`404`) with **Failed to find user(s).**
**Actor** is whoever asked (`Admin <tom@gmail.com>` or `Dev <dev@gmail.com>`), and **Target** shows a dash.
Each one has a **Stack** box holding the server's stack trace.
The refusal from tom's **Deactivate** button in R18 is among them, with **Request** `PATCH /api/users/admin/deactivate-user/<Account R1's id>`.

steps.title: Account changes in the log
do: Set **Domain** to **Users**, **Level** to **Info** and **Status** to **All statuses**.
Press **Show details** on the **Deactivate Success**, **Reactivate Success**, **Admin Delete Success** and **Get By Id Success** cards, and on both **Register Success** cards.
expect: **Register Success** appears once for each of Account R1 and Account R2, with status code `201`. Account R1's names it as both **Actor** and **Target**.
**Deactivate Success**: the message ends `targetRole=USER | isActive=false`, **Actor** is `Admin <tom@gmail.com>` and **Metadata** shows `sessionsRevoked` `true`.
**Reactivate Success**: the message ends `isActive=true`, with no **Metadata** row.
**Admin Delete Success**: the message names Account R2's id and address, **Target** is a dash, and **Metadata** holds `deletedUserId`, `email` and `role` `USER`.
**Get By Id Success**, from R11, names Account R1 as **Target** and tom as **Actor**.
Every Account R2 card is still there, but its **Target**, and the **Actor** on its **Register Success**, now show a dash.
A deleted account shows as its id followed by **(deleted)**, so it can be told apart from no account at all.
steps.note: The last check fails in practice (see found): deleting the account empties the id along with the link, so only a dash is left.

steps.title: Session and role refusals in the log
do: Clear the filters and set **Domain** to **Auth**.
Press **Show details** on each card.
expect: **no-permission** (`403`) with **This action requires an admin or developer role.** twice: from user@gmail.com in R4 (**Actor** `User <user@gmail.com>`) and from Account R1 in R13.
**no-permission** (`403`) with **This action requires a developer role.** three times: once from user@gmail.com in R4 and twice from tom in R5.
**no-validation** (`401`) with **No valid session found.** from the reloads in R21 and R24, each with a dash for **Actor**.

steps.title: Viewing logs nothing
do: Clear every filter and note the total under the list and the top card.
Reload the page three times, go to page 2 and back (if there is a page 2), try a few filters, then clear them.
Open {page:/admin/users}, search for `dev` and change **Role**, then open {page:/} and {page:/account}.
Come back to {page:/admin/events} and reload.
Paste the helper, run `await api('GET', '/api/users/admin/get-user-by-id/' + await idOf('Account R1'))`, then reload again.
expect: After all that browsing the total is exactly what you noted, and the top card is the same.
Neither list, nor the session check behind every page load, has added a card.
The single-account lookup adds one card, **Get By Id Success**, at the top: it is the one read that is logged.
steps.note: Do this while nobody else is using the server, since every other visitor's actions are logged too.

steps.title: Filters and search
do: Set **Level** to **Warning**, then to **Error**, **Critical** and **Debug** in turn.
Set **Level** to **All levels** and **Domain** to **Events**.
Set **Domain** to **All domains** and **Status** to **Open**.
Set **Status** to **All statuses**. Type `change role` in the search, then replace it with the first part of Account R1's address.
Type `nothing-matches-this`, then clear the search.
expect: **Warning** leaves only `WARNING` cards.
**Error**, **Critical** and **Debug** each show **No events match these filters.** (unless something has failed on the server), and the pager and **Delete All** disappear with the cards.
**Events** shows **No events match these filters.**, as nothing has been done to the log itself yet.
**Open** shows every card, as nothing has been triaged yet.
The search ignores case and matches either the action (`change role`) or the message (the address, which appears in messages after `targetEmail=`).
`nothing-matches-this` shows **No events match these filters.**

steps.title: Paging
do: Clear the filters. If the total is 25 or fewer, paste the helper, run `for (let i = 0; i < 30; i++) await api('PATCH', '/api/events/update-event-status/none', { status: 'DONE' });` and reload.

On page 2, set **Level** to **Warning**.
Set **Level** back to **All levels**, go to page 2 again and type `a` in the search.

Page 1 holds 25 cards and reads **Page 1 of N (T total)**, with **Previous** greyed out.
**Next** shows the next, older, events and **Page 2 of N**.
On the last page **Next** is greyed out.
Changing the level puts you back on page 1.
Typing in the search puts you back on page 1.
steps.note: The loop's events are `WARNING` **bad-request** cards in the `events` domain. Every request counts towards the server's limit of 300 per 15 minutes from one address, which all your windows share. If the server answers with a message starting **Too many requests**, restart it.

steps.title: Triage: change an event's status
do: Clear the search. On the top card, choose **Acknowledged** in its **Status** drop-down.
Choose **Resolved**, then **Ignored**.
Reload the page, then set the **Status** filter to **Ignored**.
On that card choose **Open**.
Set the **Status** filter back to **All statuses** and look at the top of the list.
expect: No dialog: each choice saves at once, with the drop-down greyed out while it does.
**Event marked Acknowledged.** in green above the list, and the badge turns to a blue `ACKNOWLEDGED`.
**Event marked Resolved.** with a green `RESOLVED` badge, then **Event marked Ignored.** with a grey `IGNORED` badge.

**Open** says **Event marked Open.** and the badge goes back to a yellow `OPEN`.

The top of the full list now holds four **Update Status Success** cards (domain `events`, `INFO`, `200`, **Actor** `Dev <dev@gmail.com>`), with messages such as `Update Status Success | eventId=<that card's id> | status=ACKNOWLEDGED`.
Those cards only appear once the list is fetched again: a status change does not refetch it.

steps.title: Acting on an event that has already gone

In the first tab, press the cross on the top card, then **Confirm**.
In the second tab, without reloading, change that same card's **Status** to **Resolved**.
Still in the second tab, press its cross and **Confirm**.
Reload the second tab.
expect: The status change shows **Failed to find event(s).** in red above the list, and the drop-down stays on **Open**.
The delete shows **Failed to find event(s).** in red too.

steps.title: Delete one event

Press its round red cross, then **Cancel**.
Press the cross again, then press **Escape**.
Tab to the cross, press Enter, Tab to **Confirm** and press Enter.
Press Tab once.
Reload the page.

**Cancel** and **Escape** leave the card in place.

The Tab after **Confirm** stays in the list rather than jumping to **Skip to main content**.

steps.title: Delete All
do: With no filters set, note the total. Then set **Level** to **Warning**.
Press **Delete All**, then **Cancel**.
Press **Delete All** again and **Confirm**.
Reload the page.
Look at the `AppEvent` model in Prisma Studio.

steps.title: Clean up: a DEVELOPER deletes Account R1
do: Check that Account R1 is still signed in in the second browser.
In the main window open {page:/admin/users}, press the cross on the Account R1 card and **Confirm**.
Reload the second browser.
Reload {page:/admin/events}.
expect: Green **Account R1 has been deleted.**, and the list shows **Dev**, **Admin** and **User**, **Page 1 of 1 (3 total)**.

The second browser's reload leaves it signed out.

parts.intro: Rules that hold on every page rather than one screen: the production build and its pre-rendering (view source, real 404s, the app shell, the hosting files, `SKIP_PRERENDER`), sitemap.xml, robots.txt, the fallback head, canonical addresses and JSON-LD, accessibility (skip link, focus on a route change, one main area, the navbar by keyboard), phone width, dark mode, analytics only after consent, the API's status page, 404s, headers, CORS and global rate limit, upload type and size checks, the orphan cleanup job, and a list of every email the site sends. Signed out throughout except C39. The build tests need the server running on a freshly seeded database, the client's production `VITE_API_URL` pointing at `http://localhost:4000` (set it yourself, for example in `client/.env.production.local`), `FRONTEND_ORIGIN` on the server including `http://localhost:4173`, and Chromium for the pre-render (`npx playwright install chromium` in `client/`, once). Then run `npm run build` and `npm run preview` in `client/`. What this part changes: the build output in `client/dist/` (C3 also edits a source file for a moment: undo it), test uploads under the bucket's `testing/` folder and their `MediaItem` rows (C45 removes them with `npm run media:cleanup -- --hours 0`), one closed booking day (C39) and the in-memory rate-limit counters (restart the server to clear them). curl commands are for Windows PowerShell, so type `curl.exe`: plain `curl` is a PowerShell alias. Run the browser checks in Chrome. On a fresh profile the cookie modal opens after ten seconds and holds the keyboard focus, so accept it first unless the test is about it. Where the site's own text contains a dash, the quotes here split at it.

steps.title: The production build passes
do: In `server/`, reseed with `npx prisma db seed` and start the API with `npm start`.
Make sure the client's production `VITE_API_URL` is `http://localhost:4000` and Chromium for Playwright is installed (see the intro).
In `client/` run `npm run build` and read the output from the top.
List the files in `client/dist/` and `client/dist/blog/`.
expect: Before Vite starts, the meta check prints **Page meta check passed (12 indexable pages)**.
After Vite's own output: **Inlined critical CSS into 1 HTML file(s)**.

One **Pre-rendered** line per address, in this order: `/`, `/about`, `/reviews`, `/gallery`, `/faq`, `/contact`, `/links`, `/blog`, `/guest-book`, `/booking`, `/newsletter`, `/user-agreements`, `/blog/welcome-to-the-blog`, `/__prerender-404__`. None has a warning after it.
Then **Pre-rendered 12 pages, 1 blog posts and 404.html for https://bytetoast-studio.com**.
Then **sitemap.xml generated at dist/sitemap.xml (12 static routes, 1 blog posts)** and **robots.txt generated at dist/robots.txt**.
Last comes **SEO check passed (13 pages in dist/)** with no **thin page** warning above it, and the command ends without an error.

`dist/` holds `index.html`, one `.html` file for each other public page (`about.html` to `user-agreements.html`), `404.html`, `app-shell.html`, `_redirects`, `.htaccess`, `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt`.
`dist/blog/` holds `welcome-to-the-blog.html` and no `draft-post.html`.
steps.note: The pre-render serves the build on port 4175 and walks every page in headless Chromium, so the API must be up for the reviews, guest book, blog and booking data to be saved into the HTML. The seed has one published post (`welcome-to-the-blog`) and one draft (`draft-post`).

steps.title: Building while the API is down
do: Stop the server and run `npm run build` in `client/` again.
Open `client/dist/sitemap.xml` and list `client/dist/`.
Start the server again and run `npm run build` once more before the next tests.
expect: A warning starting **Could not reach the backend (VITE_API_URL) to list blog posts** appears twice: once for the pre-render and once for the sitemap.
The **Pre-rendered** lines for `/`, `/reviews`, `/blog`, `/guest-book` and `/booking` end with a count and **API request(s) failed, check the saved page**.
The summary reads **Pre-rendered 12 pages, 0 blog posts and 404.html for https://bytetoast-studio.com** and the sitemap line ends **(12 static routes, 0 blog posts)**.
The sitemap lists the 12 public pages with no `<lastmod>` anywhere, and there is no `dist/blog/` folder.
The build still reaches the SEO check; any **thin page** warning names a page whose data did not load.
After the last build, with the server up, the warnings are gone and C1's output is back.
steps.note: If a page's main area holds under 40 characters, the SEO check fails instead, with a line containing **main content is only**.

steps.title: What a failed build looks like
do: In a second terminal in `client/`, run `npm run preview -- --port 4175` (the pre-render's own port), then run `npm run build` in the first terminal. Stop the second preview afterwards.
Change the About entry's `desc` in `client/src/utils/data/helmetData.js` to `Short.`, run `npm run check:meta`, then undo the change.

steps.title: The hosting rules: _redirects and .htaccess
do: Open `client/dist/_redirects` in an editor.
Open `client/dist/.htaccess` and search for `__CLIENT_ONLY_REWRITES__` and `app-shell`.
Open `client/public/.htaccess` and search for the same marker.
expect: `_redirects` starts `# Written by scripts/prerender.mjs`, then has two lines for each browser-only prefix, such as `/admin  /app-shell.html  200` and `/admin/*  /app-shell.html  200`.

That makes 22 rule lines, for `/admin`, `/account`, `/blog`, `/login`, `/sign-up`, `/forgot-password`, `/verify-email-address`, `/reset-password`, `/newsletter/sign-up-success`, `/newsletter/unsubscribe` and `/down-for-maintenance`.
There is no catch-all `/*` line: the pre-rendered files are served first and Netlify serves `404.html` for anything else.

In `dist/.htaccess` the marker is gone. In its place: `RewriteRule ^(admin|account|blog|login|sign-up|forgot-password|verify-email-address|reset-password|newsletter/sign-up-success|newsletter/unsubscribe|down-for-maintenance)(/.*)?$ /app-shell.html [L]`.
Above it sit the rules that send `/about/` to `/about` with a 301 and serve `/about` from `about.html`; after the block comes `ErrorDocument 404 /404.html`.
`client/public/.htaccess`, the source, still holds `#__CLIENT_ONLY_REWRITES__`: only the copy in `dist/` is filled in.
steps.note: Neither set of rules has been tried on a real Netlify build or cPanel host yet (`documents/site/SiteInfo.md`).

Enter on the toggle opens the panel, the icon becomes a cross and `aria-expanded` is `true`; Tab then walks **Home** to **Sign Up**, and **Legal** opens its three links on Enter.
Enter on the toggle again closes the panel and `aria-expanded` is `false`.
steps.note: Known fault (found): the closed menu is only made transparent, so Tab walks through its invisible links and screen readers read them. The menu itself is in the public part.

steps.title: The automated checks: e2e and Lighthouse

steps.title: No sideways scroll at 375px

expect: `375` on every page, and nothing moves sideways.
Text wraps inside the screen and images shrink to fit; nothing is cut off at the right edge.
The navbar shows the logo and the menu button only.
On /user-agreements the legal text takes the full width, with the contents list above it or out of the way.
steps.note: Known fault (found): /user-agreements keeps its 256px contents list beside the text and scrolls sideways. The sign-in and password pages are in C29.

steps.title: Sign-in and password pages on a small phone

steps.title: Dark mode follows the system
